units.leftText: Many have undertaken to compose an account of the things that have been fulfilled among us,
units.rightText: Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to draw up a narrative concerning those matters which have been fulfilled among us,

units.leftText: just as they were handed down to us by the initial eyewitnesses and servants of the word.
units.rightText: even as they delivered them unto us, who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word,

units.leftText: Therefore, having carefully investigated everything from the beginning, it seemed good also to me to write an orderly account for you, most excellent Theophilus,
units.rightText: it seemed good to me also, having traced the course of all things accurately from the first, to write unto thee in order, most excellent Theophilus;

units.leftText: In the time of Herod king of Judea there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah, and whose wife Elizabeth was a descendant of Aaron.
units.rightText: There was in the days of Herod, king of Judæa, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abijah: and he had a wife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.

units.leftText: Both of them were righteous in the sight of God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and decrees of the Lord.
units.rightText: And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.

units.leftText: But they had no children, because Elizabeth was barren, and they were both well along in years.
units.rightText: And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they both were now well stricken in years.

units.leftText: One day while Zechariah’s division was on duty and he was serving as priest before God,
units.rightText: Now it came to pass, while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his course,

units.leftText: he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to enter the temple of the Lord and burn incense.
units.rightText: according to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to enter into the temple of the Lord and burn incense.

units.leftText: And at the hour of the incense offering, the whole congregation was praying outside.
units.rightText: And the whole multitude of the people were praying without at the hour of incense.

units.leftText: Just then an angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.
units.rightText: And there appeared unto him an angel of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of incense.

units.leftText: When Zechariah saw him, he was startled and gripped with fear.
units.rightText: And Zacharias was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.

units.leftText: But the angel said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to give him the name John.
units.rightText: But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: because thy supplication is heard, and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.

units.leftText: He will be a joy and delight to you, and many will rejoice at his birth,
units.rightText: And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth.

units.leftText: for he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He shall never take wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb.
units.rightText: For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and he shall drink no wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother’s womb.

units.leftText: Many of the sons of Israel he will turn back to the Lord their God.
units.rightText: And many of the children of Israel shall he turn unto the Lord their God.

units.leftText: And he will go on before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to their children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous — to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.”
units.rightText: And he shall go before his face in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to walk in the wisdom of the just; to make ready for the Lord a people prepared for him.

units.leftText: “How can I be sure of this?” Zechariah asked the angel. “I am an old man, and my wife is well along in years.”
units.rightText: And Zacharias said unto the angel, Whereby shall I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife well stricken in years.

units.leftText: “I am Gabriel,” replied the angel. “I stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.
units.rightText: And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God; and I was sent to speak unto thee, and to bring thee these good tidings.

units.leftText: And now you will be silent and unable to speak until the day this comes to pass, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their proper time.”
units.rightText: And behold, thou shalt be silent and not able to speak, until the day that these things shall come to pass, because thou believedst not my words, which shall be fulfilled in their season.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, the people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering why he took so long in the temple.
units.rightText: And the people were waiting for Zacharias, and they marvelled while he tarried in the temple.

units.leftText: When he came out and was unable to speak to them, they realized he had seen a vision in the temple. He kept making signs to them but remained unable to speak.
units.rightText: And when he came out, he could not speak unto them: and they perceived that he had seen a vision in the temple: and he continued making signs unto them, and remained dumb.

units.leftText: And when the days of his service were complete, he returned home.

units.leftText: When His parents saw Him, they were astonished. “Child, why have You done this to us?” His mother asked. “Your father and I have been anxiously searching for You.”
units.rightText: And when they saw him, they were astonished; and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I sought thee sorrowing.

units.leftText: “Why were you looking for Me?” He asked. “Did you not know that I had to be in My Father’s house ?”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? knew ye not that I must be in my Father’s house?
leftNotes: 2:49 Or I had to be about My Father’s business

units.leftText: But they did not understand the statement He was making to them.
units.rightText: And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them.

units.leftText: Then He went down to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them. But His mother treasured up all these things in her heart.
units.rightText: And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth; and he was subject unto them: and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.

units.leftText: And Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man.
units.rightText: And Jesus advanced in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.

units.leftText: In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, while Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
units.rightText: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Cæsar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judæa, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituræa and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,

units.leftText: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
units.rightText: in the high-priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came unto John the son of Zacharias in the wilderness.

units.leftText: He went into all the region around the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,
units.rightText: And he came into all the region round about the Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance unto remission of sins;

units.leftText: as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.
units.rightText: as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make ye ready the way of the Lord, Make his paths straight.

units.leftText: Every valley shall be filled in, and every mountain and hill made low. The crooked ways shall be made straight, and the rough ways smooth.
units.rightText: Every valley shall be filled, And every mountain and hill shall be brought low; And the crooked shall become straight, And the rough ways smooth;

units.leftText: And all humanity will see God’s salvation.’”
units.rightText: And all flesh shall see the salvation of God.
leftNotes: 3:6 Literally And all flesh will see God’s salvation; Isaiah 40:3–5|ISA 40:3-5* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Then John said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, “You brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
units.rightText: He said therefore to the multitudes that went out to be baptized of him, Ye offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

units.leftText: Produce fruit, then, in keeping with repentance. And do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.
units.rightText: Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.

units.leftText: The axe lies ready at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.”
units.rightText: And even now the axe also lieth at the root of the trees: every tree therefore that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

units.leftText: The crowds asked him, “What then should we do?”
units.rightText: And the multitudes asked him, saying, What then must we do?

units.leftText: John replied, “Whoever has two tunics should share with him who has none, and whoever has food should do the same.”
units.rightText: And he answered and said unto them, He that hath two coats, let him impart to him that hath none; and he that hath food, let him do likewise.

units.leftText: Even tax collectors came to be baptized. “Teacher,” they asked, “what should we do?”
units.rightText: And there came also publicans to be baptized, and they said unto him, Teacher, what must we do?

units.leftText: “Collect no more than you are authorized,” he answered.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Extort no more than that which is appointed you.

units.leftText: Then some soldiers asked him, “And what should we do?” “Do not take money by force or false accusation,” he said. “Be content with your wages.”
units.rightText: And soldiers also asked him, saying, And we, what must we do? And he said unto them, Extort from no man by violence, neither accuse any one wrongfully; and be content with your wages.

units.leftText: The people were waiting expectantly and were all wondering in their hearts if John could be the Christ.
units.rightText: And as the people were in expectation, and all men reasoned in their hearts concerning John, whether haply he were the Christ;

units.leftText: John answered all of them: “I baptize you with water, but One more powerful than I will come, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
units.rightText: John answered, saying unto them all, I indeed baptize you with water; but there cometh he that is mightier than I, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose: he shall baptize you in the Holy Spirit and in fire:
leftNotes: 3:16 Or in water
3:16 Cited in Acts 13:25|ACT 13:25*
3:16 Or in the Holy Spirit and in fire

units.leftText: His winnowing fork is in His hand to clear His threshing floor and to gather the wheat into His barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
units.rightText: whose fan is in his hand, thoroughly to cleanse his threshing-floor, and to gather the wheat into his garner; but the chaff he will burn up with unquenchable fire.

units.leftText: With these and many other exhortations, John proclaimed the good news to the people.
units.rightText: With many other exhortations therefore preached he good tidings unto the people;

units.leftText: But when he rebuked Herod the tetrarch regarding his brother’s wife Herodias and all the evils he had done,
units.rightText: but Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him for Herodias his brother’s wife, and for all the evil things which Herod had done,

units.leftText: Herod added this to them all: He locked John up in prison. The Baptism of Jesus (Matthew 3:13–17|MAT 3:13-17*; Mark 1:9–11|MRK 1:9-11*; John 1:29–34|JHN 1:29-34*)
units.rightText: added this also to them all, that he shut up John in prison.

units.leftText: When all the people were being baptized, Jesus was baptized too. And as He was praying, heaven was opened,
units.rightText: Now it came to pass, when all the people were baptized, that, Jesus also having been baptized, and praying, the heaven was opened,

units.leftText: and the Holy Spirit descended on Him in a bodily form like a dove. And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.” The Genealogy of Jesus (Ruth 4:18–22|RUT 4:18-22*; Matthew 1:1–17|MAT 1:1-17*)
units.rightText: and the Holy Spirit descended in a bodily form, as a dove, upon him, and a voice came out of heaven, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.

units.rightText: And Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years of age, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

units.rightText: the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,

units.rightText: the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Josech, the son of Joda,

units.rightText: the son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,

units.rightText: the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan,

units.leftText: Then Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,
units.rightText: And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan, and was led in the Spirit in the wilderness
leftNotes: 4:1 Or in the wilderness

units.leftText: where for forty days He was tempted by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and when they had ended, He was hungry.
units.rightText: during forty days, being tempted of the devil. And he did eat nothing in those days: and when they were completed, he hungered.

units.leftText: The devil said to Him, “If You are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread.”
units.rightText: And the devil said unto him, If thou art the Son of God, command this stone that it become bread.

units.leftText: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone.’ ”
units.rightText: And Jesus answered unto him, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone.
leftNotes: 4:4 Deuteronomy 8:3|DEU 8:3*; BYZ and TR on bread alone, but on every word of God.

units.leftText: Then the devil led Him up to a high place and showed Him in an instant all the kingdoms of the world.
units.rightText: And he led him up, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.

units.leftText: “I will give You authority over all these kingdoms and all their glory,” he said. “For it has been relinquished to me, and I can give it to anyone I wish.
units.rightText: And the devil said unto him, To thee will I give all this authority, and the glory of them: for it hath been delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.

units.leftText: So if You worship me, it will all be Yours.”
units.rightText: If thou therefore wilt worship before me, it shall all be thine.

units.leftText: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’ ”
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said unto him, It is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
leftNotes: 4:8 Deuteronomy 6:13|DEU 6:13*; BYZ and TR “Get behind Me, Satan! For it is written...

units.leftText: Then the devil led Him to Jerusalem and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple. “If You are the Son of God,” he said, “throw Yourself down from here.
units.rightText: And he led him to Jerusalem, and set him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou art the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence:

units.leftText: For it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning You to guard You carefully,
units.rightText: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning thee, to guard thee:

units.leftText: and they will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.’ ”
units.rightText: and, On their hands they shall bear thee up, Lest haply thou dash thy foot against a stone.

units.leftText: But Jesus answered, “It also says, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’ ”
units.rightText: And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not make trial of the Lord thy God.
leftNotes: 4:12 Deuteronomy 6:16|DEU 6:16*

units.leftText: When the devil had finished every temptation, he left Him until an opportune time. Jesus Begins His Ministry (Isaiah 9:1–7|ISA 9:1-7*; Matthew 4:12–17|MAT 4:12-17*; Mark 1:14–15|MRK 1:14-15*)
units.rightText: And when the devil had completed every temptation, he departed from him for a season.

units.leftText: Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and the news about Him spread throughout the surrounding region.
units.rightText: And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee: and a fame went out concerning him through all the region round about.

units.leftText: He taught in their synagogues and was glorified by everyone. The Rejection at Nazareth (Isaiah 61:1–11|ISA 61:1-11*; Matthew 13:53–58|MAT 13:53-58*; Mark 6:1–6|MRK 6:1-6*)
units.rightText: And he taught in their synagogues, being glorified of all.

units.leftText: Then Jesus came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up. As was His custom, He entered the synagogue on the Sabbath. And when He stood up to read,
units.rightText: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and he entered, as his custom was, into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up to read.

units.leftText: the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Him. Unrolling it, He found the place where it was written:
units.rightText: And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Isaiah. And he opened the book, and found the place where it was written,

units.leftText: “The Spirit of the Lord is on Me, because He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to release the oppressed,
units.rightText: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, Because he anointed me to preach good tidings to the poor: He hath sent me to proclaim release to the captives, And recovering of sight to the blind, To set at liberty them that are bruised,
leftNotes: 4:18 BYZ and TR He has sent Me to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives

units.leftText: to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.”
units.rightText: To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.
leftNotes: 4:19 Or to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord; Isaiah 61:1–2|ISA 61:1-2* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Then He rolled up the scroll, returned it to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on Him,
units.rightText: And he closed the book, and gave it back to the attendant, and sat down: and the eyes of all in the synagogue were fastened on him.

units.leftText: and He began by saying, “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”
units.rightText: And he began to say unto them, To-day hath this scripture been fulfilled in your ears.

units.leftText: All spoke well of Him and marveled at the gracious words that came from His lips. “Isn’t this the son of Joseph?” they asked.
units.rightText: And all bare him witness, and wondered at the words of grace which proceeded out of his mouth: and they said, Is not this Joseph’s son?

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “Surely you will quote this proverb to Me: ‘Physician, heal yourself! Do here in Your hometown what we have heard that You did in Capernaum.’”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Doubtless ye will say unto me this parable, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done at Capernaum, do also here in thine own country.

units.leftText: Then He added, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.
units.rightText: And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is acceptable in his own country.

units.leftText: But I tell you truthfully that there were many widows in Israel in the time of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three and a half years and great famine swept over all the land.
units.rightText: But of a truth I say unto you, There were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when there came a great famine over all the land;

units.leftText: Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon.
units.rightText: and unto none of them was Elijah sent, but only to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.

units.leftText: And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet. Yet not one of them was cleansed— only Naaman the Syrian.”
units.rightText: And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, but only Naaman the Syrian.
leftNotes: 4:27 A leper was one afflicted with a skin disease. See Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: On hearing this, all the people in the synagogue were enraged.
units.rightText: And they were all filled with wrath in the synagogue, as they heard these things;

units.leftText: They got up, drove Him out of the town, and led Him to the brow of the hill on which the town was built, in order to throw Him over the cliff.
units.rightText: and they rose up, and cast him forth out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might throw him down headlong.

units.leftText: But Jesus passed through the crowd and went on His way. Jesus Expels an Unclean Spirit (Mark 1:21–28|MRK 1:21-28*)
units.rightText: But he passing through the midst of them went his way.

units.leftText: Then He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and on the Sabbath He began to teach the people.
units.rightText: And he came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee. And he was teaching them on the sabbath day:

units.leftText: They were astonished at His teaching, because His message had authority.
units.rightText: and they were astonished at his teaching; for his word was with authority.

units.leftText: In the synagogue there was a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon. He cried out in a loud voice,
units.rightText: And in the synagogue there was a man, that had a spirit of an unclean demon; and he cried out with a loud voice,

units.leftText: “Ha! What do You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are — the Holy One of God!”
units.rightText: Ah! what have we to do with thee, Jesus thou Nazarene? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.

units.leftText: But Jesus rebuked the demon. “Be silent!” He said. “Come out of him!” At this, the demon threw the man down before them all and came out without harming him.
units.rightText: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him. And when the demon had thrown him down in the midst, he came out of him, having done him no hurt.

units.leftText: All the people were overcome with amazement and asked one another, “What is this message? With authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”
units.rightText: And amazement came upon all, and they spake together, one with another, saying, What is this word? for with authority and power he commandeth the unclean spirits, and they come out.

units.leftText: And the news about Jesus spread throughout the surrounding region. Jesus Heals at Peter’s House (Matthew 8:14–17|MAT 8:14-17*; Mark 1:29–34|MRK 1:29-34*)
units.rightText: And there went forth a rumor concerning him into every place of the region round about.

units.leftText: After Jesus had left the synagogue, He went to the home of Simon, whose mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever. So they appealed to Jesus on her behalf,
units.rightText: And he rose up from the synagogue, and entered into the house of Simon. And Simon’s wife’s mother was holden with a great fever; and they besought him for her.

units.leftText: and He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. And she got up at once and began to serve them.
units.rightText: And he stood over her, and rebuked the fever; and it left her: and immediately she rose up and ministered unto them.

units.leftText: At sunset, all who were ill with various diseases were brought to Jesus, and laying His hands on each one, He healed them.
units.rightText: And when the sun was setting, all they that had any sick with divers diseases brought them unto him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.

units.leftText: Demons also came out of many people, shouting, “You are the Son of God!” But He rebuked the demons and would not allow them to speak, because they knew He was the Christ. Jesus Preaches in Judea (Mark 1:35–39|MRK 1:35-39*)
units.rightText: And demons also came out from many, crying out, and saying, Thou art the Son of God. And rebuking them, he suffered them not to speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.

units.leftText: At daybreak, Jesus went out to a solitary place, and the crowds were looking for Him. They came to Him and tried to keep Him from leaving.
units.rightText: And when it was day, he came out and went into a desert place: and the multitudes sought after him, and came unto him, and would have stayed him, that he should not go from them.

units.leftText: But Jesus told them, “I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well, because that is why I was sent.”
units.rightText: But he said unto them, I must preach the good tidings of the kingdom of God to the other cities also: for therefore was I sent.

units.leftText: And He continued to preach in the synagogues of Judea.
units.rightText: And he was preaching in the synagogues of Galilee.
leftNotes: 4:44 BYZ and TR Galilee; see Mark 1:39|MRK 1:39*.

units.leftText: On one occasion, while Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on Him to hear the word of God,
units.rightText: Now it came to pass, while the multitude pressed upon him and heard the word of God, that he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret;
leftNotes: 5:1 That is, the Sea of Galilee

units.leftText: He saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.
units.rightText: and he saw two boats standing by the lake: but the fishermen had gone out of them, and were washing their nets.

units.leftText: Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon and asked him to put out a little from shore. And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.
units.rightText: And he entered into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, and asked him to put out a little from the land. And he sat down and taught the multitudes out of the boat.

units.leftText: When Jesus had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”
units.rightText: And when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.

units.leftText: “Master,” Simon replied, “we have worked hard all night without catching anything. But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”
units.rightText: And Simon answered and said, Master, we toiled all night, and took nothing: but at thy word I will let down the nets.

units.leftText: When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.
units.rightText: And when they had done this, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes; and their nets were breaking;

units.leftText: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
units.rightText: and they beckoned unto their partners in the other boat, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the boats, so that they began to sink.

units.leftText: When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees. “Go away from me, Lord,” he said, “for I am a sinful man.”
units.rightText: But Simon Peter, when he saw it, fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.

units.leftText: For he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken,
units.rightText: For he was amazed, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken;

units.leftText: and so were his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee.
units.rightText: and so were also James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.

units.leftText: And when they had brought their boats ashore, they left everything and followed Him. The Leper’s Prayer (Leviticus 14:1–32|LEV 14:1-32*; Matthew 8:1–4|MAT 8:1-4*; Mark 1:40–45|MRK 1:40-45*)
units.rightText: And when they had brought their boats to land, they left all, and followed him.

units.leftText: While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man came along who was covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown and begged Him, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, while he was in one of the cities, behold, a man full of leprosy: and when he saw Jesus, he fell on his face, and besought him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
leftNotes: 5:12 Leprosy was a term used for various skin diseases. See Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!” And immediately the leprosy left him.
units.rightText: And he stretched forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will; be thou made clean. And straightway the leprosy departed from him.

units.leftText: “Do not tell anyone,” Jesus instructed him. “But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”
units.rightText: And he charged him to tell no man: but go thy way, and show thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
leftNotes: 5:14 See Leviticus 14:1–32|LEV 14:1-32*.

units.leftText: But the news about Jesus spread all the more, and great crowds came to hear Him and to be healed of their sicknesses.
units.rightText: But so much the more went abroad the report concerning him: and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed of their infirmities.

units.leftText: Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray. Jesus Heals a Paralytic (Matthew 9:1–8|MAT 9:1-8*; Mark 2:1–12|MRK 2:1-12*)
units.rightText: But he withdrew himself in the deserts, and prayed.

units.leftText: One day Jesus was teaching, and the Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. People had come from Jerusalem and from every village of Galilee and Judea, and the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal the sick.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on one of those days, that he was teaching; and there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, who were come out of every village of Galilee and Judæa and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was with him to heal.

units.leftText: Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him inside to set him before Jesus,
units.rightText: And behold, men bring on a bed a man that was palsied: and they sought to bring him in, and to lay him before him.

units.leftText: but they could not find a way through the crowd. So they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.
units.rightText: And not finding by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went up to the housetop, and let him down through the tiles with his couch into the midst before Jesus.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw their faith, He said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.”
units.rightText: And seeing their faith, he said, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.

units.leftText: But the scribes and Pharisees began thinking to themselves, “Who is this man who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
units.rightText: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this that speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?

units.leftText: Knowing what they were thinking, Jesus replied, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
units.rightText: But Jesus perceiving their reasonings, answered and said unto them, Why reason ye in your hearts?

units.leftText: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
units.rightText: Which is easier, to say, Thy sins are forgiven thee; or to say, Arise and walk?

units.leftText: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins…” He said to the paralytic, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
units.rightText: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath authority on earth to forgive sins (he said unto him that was palsied), I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go unto thy house.

units.leftText: And immediately the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.
units.rightText: And immediately he rose up before them, and took up that whereon he lay, and departed to his house, glorifying God.

units.leftText: Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God. They were filled with awe and said, “We have seen remarkable things today.” Jesus Calls Levi (Matthew 9:9–13|MAT 9:9-13*; Mark 2:13–17|MRK 2:13-17*)
units.rightText: And amazement took hold on all, and they glorified God; and they were filled with fear, saying, We have seen strange things to-day.

units.leftText: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him,
units.rightText: And after these things he went forth, and beheld a publican, named Levi, sitting at the place of toll, and said unto him, Follow me.

units.leftText: and Levi got up, left everything, and followed Him.
units.rightText: And he forsook all, and rose up and followed him.

units.leftText: Then Levi hosted a great banquet for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors was there, along with others who were eating with them.
units.rightText: And Levi made him a great feast in his house: and there was a great multitude of publicans and of others that were sitting at meat with them.

units.leftText: But the Pharisees and their scribes complained to Jesus’ disciples, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
units.rightText: And the Pharisees and their scribes murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with the publicans and sinners?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.
units.rightText: And Jesus answering said unto them, They that are in health have no need of a physician; but they that are sick.

units.leftText: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.” Questions about Fasting (Matthew 9:14–15|MAT 9:14-15*; Mark 2:18–20|MRK 2:18-20*)
units.rightText: I am not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.

units.leftText: Then they said to Him, “John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray, but Yours keep on eating and drinking.”
units.rightText: And they said unto him, The disciples of John fast often, and make supplications; likewise also the disciples of the Pharisees; but thine eat and drink.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, Can ye make the sons of the bride-chamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?

units.leftText: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.” The Patches and the Wineskins (Matthew 9:16–17|MAT 9:16-17*; Mark 2:21–22|MRK 2:21-22*)
units.rightText: But the days will come; and when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, then will they fast in those days.

units.leftText: He also told them a parable: “No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment as well, and the patch from the new will not match the old.
units.rightText: And he spake also a parable unto them: No man rendeth a piece from a new garment and putteth it upon an old garment; else he will rend the new, and also the piece from the new will not agree with the old.

units.leftText: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.
units.rightText: And no man putteth new wine into old wine-skins; else the new wine will burst the skins, and itself will be spilled, and the skins will perish.

units.leftText: Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.
units.rightText: But new wine must be put into fresh wine-skins.

units.leftText: And no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”
units.rightText: And no man having drunk old wine desireth new; for he saith, The old is good.

units.leftText: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them.
units.rightText: Now it came to pass on a sabbath, that he was going through the grainfields; and his disciples plucked the ears, and did eat, rubbing them in their hands.
leftNotes: 6:1 BYZ and TR On the second Sabbath after the first

units.leftText: But some of the Pharisees asked, “Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”
units.rightText: But certain of the Pharisees said, Why do ye that which it is not lawful to do on the sabbath day?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
units.rightText: And Jesus answering them said, Have ye not read even this, what David did, when he was hungry, he, and they that were with him;

units.leftText: He entered the house of God, took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions, and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat.”
units.rightText: how he entered into the house of God, and took and ate the showbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat save for the priests alone?
leftNotes: 6:4 Or the Bread of the Presence

units.leftText: Then Jesus declared, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.” Jesus Heals on the Sabbath (Matthew 12:9–14|MAT 12:9-14*; Mark 3:1–6|MRK 3:1-6*)
units.rightText: And he said unto them, The Son of man is lord of the sabbath.

units.leftText: On another Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was withered.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue and taught: and there was a man there, and his right hand was withered.

units.leftText: Looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, the scribes and Pharisees were watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.
units.rightText: And the scribes and the Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the sabbath; that they might find how to accuse him.

units.leftText: But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand among us.” So he got up and stood there.
units.rightText: But he knew their thoughts; and he said to the man that had his hand withered, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose and stood forth.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, I ask you, Is it lawful on the sabbath to do good, or to do harm? to save a life, or to destroy it?

units.leftText: And after looking around at all of them, He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and it was restored.
units.rightText: And he looked round about on them all, and said unto him, Stretch forth thy hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored.

units.leftText: But the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus. The Twelve Apostles (Matthew 10:1–4|MAT 10:1-4*; Mark 3:13–19|MRK 3:13-19*)
units.rightText: But they were filled with madness; and communed one with another what they might do to Jesus.

units.leftText: In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and He spent the night in prayer to God.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in these days, that he went out into the mountain to pray; and he continued all night in prayer to God.

units.leftText: When daylight came, He called His disciples to Him and chose twelve of them, whom He also designated as apostles:
units.rightText: And when it was day, he called his disciples; and he chose from them twelve, whom also he named apostles:

units.leftText: Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;
units.rightText: Simon, whom he also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, and James and John, and Philip and Bartholomew,

units.leftText: Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot;
units.rightText: and Matthew and Thomas, and James the son of Alphæus, and Simon who was called the Zealot,

units.leftText: Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor. Jesus Heals the Multitudes (Matthew 4:23–25|MAT 4:23-25*; Mark 3:7–12|MRK 3:7-12*)
units.rightText: and Judas the son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor;

units.leftText: Then Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of His disciples was there, along with a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon.
units.rightText: and he came down with them, and stood on a level place, and a great multitude of his disciples, and a great number of the people from all Judæa and Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;

units.leftText: They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases, and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.
units.rightText: and they that were troubled with unclean spirits were healed.

units.leftText: The entire crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was coming from Him and healing them all. The Beatitudes (Psalm 1:1–6|PSA 1:1-6*; Matthew 5:3–12|MAT 5:3-12*)
units.rightText: And all the multitude sought to touch him; for power came forth from him, and healed them all.

units.leftText: Looking up at His disciples, Jesus said: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
units.rightText: And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed are ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
units.rightText: Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shall be filled. Blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh.

units.leftText: Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
units.rightText: Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake.

units.leftText: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way. Woes to the Satisfied (Amos 6:1–7|AMO 6:1-7*)
units.rightText: Rejoice in that day, and leap for joy: for behold, your reward is great in heaven; for in the same manner did their fathers unto the prophets.

units.leftText: But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.
units.rightText: But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.

units.leftText: Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
units.rightText: Woe unto you, ye that are full now! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you, ye that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.

units.leftText: Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way. Love Your Enemies (Matthew 5:38–48|MAT 5:38-48*)
units.rightText: Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for in the same manner did their fathers to the false prophets.

units.leftText: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
units.rightText: But I say unto you that hear, Love your enemies, do good to them that hate you,

units.leftText: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
units.rightText: bless them that curse you, pray for them that despitefully use you.

units.leftText: If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also. And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.
units.rightText: To him that smiteth thee on the one cheek offer also the other; and from him that taketh away thy cloak withhold not thy coat also.

units.leftText: Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.
units.rightText: Give to every one that asketh thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask them not again.

units.leftText: Do to others as you would have them do to you.
units.rightText: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.

units.leftText: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.
units.rightText: And if ye love them that love you, what thank have ye? for even sinners love those that love them.

units.leftText: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.
units.rightText: And if ye do good to them that do good to you, what thank have ye? for even sinners do the same.

units.leftText: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.
units.rightText: And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? even sinners lend to sinners, to receive again as much.

units.leftText: But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.
units.rightText: But love your enemies, and do them good, and lend, never despairing; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be sons of the Most High: for he is kind toward the unthankful and evil.

units.leftText: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful. Judging Others (Matthew 7:1–6|MAT 7:1-6*; Romans 14:1–12|ROM 14:1-12*)
units.rightText: Be ye merciful, even as your Father is merciful.

units.leftText: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
units.rightText: And judge not, and ye shall not be judged: and condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: release, and ye shall be released:

units.leftText: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”
units.rightText: give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, shaken together, running over, shall they give into your bosom. For with what measure ye mete it shall be measured to you again.

units.leftText: Jesus also told them a parable: “Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?
units.rightText: And he spake also a parable unto them, Can the blind guide the blind? shall they not both fall into a pit?

units.leftText: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
units.rightText: The disciple is not above his teacher: but every one when he is perfected shall be as his teacher.

units.leftText: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?
units.rightText: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

units.leftText: How can you say, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye. A Tree and Its Fruit (Matthew 7:15–23|MAT 7:15-23*; Matthew 12:33–37|MAT 12:33-37*)
units.rightText: Or how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me cast out the mote that is in thine eye, when thou thyself beholdest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote that is in thy brother’s eye.

units.leftText: No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.
units.rightText: For there is no good tree that bringeth forth corrupt fruit; nor again a corrupt tree that bringeth forth good fruit.

units.leftText: For each tree is known by its own fruit. Indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles.
units.rightText: For each tree is known by its own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.

units.leftText: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks. The House on the Rock (Matthew 7:24–27|MAT 7:24-27*)
units.rightText: The good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and the evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth that which is evil: for out of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.

units.leftText: Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but do not do what I say?
units.rightText: And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?

units.leftText: I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them:
units.rightText: Every one that cometh unto me, and heareth my words, and doeth them, I will show you to whom he is like:

units.leftText: He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.
units.rightText: he is like a man building a house, who digged and went deep, and laid a foundation upon the rock: and when a flood arose, the stream brake against that house, and could not shake it: because it had been well builded.
leftNotes: 6:48 BYZ and TR because its foundation was on the rock; see Matthew 7:25|MAT 7:25*.

units.leftText: But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell — and great was its destruction!”
units.rightText: But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that built a house upon the earth without a foundation; against which the stream brake, and straightway it fell in; and the ruin of that house was great.

units.leftText: When Jesus had concluded His discourse in the hearing of the people, He went to Capernaum.
units.rightText: After he had ended all his sayings in the ears of the people, he entered into Capernaum.

units.leftText: There a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die.
units.rightText: And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick and at the point of death.

units.leftText: When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to ask Him to come and heal his servant.
units.rightText: And when he heard concerning Jesus, he sent unto him elders of the Jews, asking him that he would come and save his servant.

units.leftText: They came to Jesus and pleaded with Him earnestly, “This man is worthy to have You grant this,
units.rightText: And they, when they came to Jesus, besought him earnestly, saying, He is worthy that thou shouldest do this for him;

units.leftText: for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue.”
units.rightText: for he loveth our nation, and himself built us our synagogue.

units.leftText: So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.
units.rightText: And Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself; for I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof:

units.leftText: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
units.rightText: wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say the word, and my servant shall be healed.

units.leftText: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”
units.rightText: For I also am a man set under authority, having under myself soldiers: and I say to this one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.

units.leftText: When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”
units.rightText: And when Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned and said unto the multitude that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

units.leftText: And when the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant in good health. Jesus Raises a Widow’s Son
units.rightText: And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole.

units.leftText: Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd.
units.rightText: And it came to pass soon afterwards, that he went to a city called Nain; and his disciples went with him, and a great multitude.

units.leftText: As He approached the town gate, He saw a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And a large crowd from the town was with her.
units.rightText: Now when he drew near to the gate of the city, behold, there was carried out one that was dead, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her.

units.leftText: When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her and said, “Do not weep.”
units.rightText: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.

units.leftText: Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. “Young man,” He said, “I tell you, get up!”
units.rightText: And he came nigh and touched the bier: and the bearers stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.
leftNotes: 7:14 Literally bier, probably a wooden plank or open coffin

units.leftText: And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.
units.rightText: And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he gave him to his mother.

units.leftText: A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God. “A great prophet has appeared among us!” they said. “God has visited His people!”
units.rightText: And fear took hold on all: and they glorified God, saying, A great prophet is arisen among us: and, God hath visited his people.

units.leftText: And the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region. John’s Inquiry (Matthew 11:1–6|MAT 11:1-6*)
units.rightText: And this report went forth concerning him in the whole of Judæa, and all the region round about.

units.leftText: Then John’s disciples informed him about all these things.
units.rightText: And the disciples of John told him of all these things.

units.leftText: So John called two of his disciples and sent them to ask the Lord, “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”
units.rightText: And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to the Lord, saying, Art thou he that cometh, or look we for another?

units.leftText: When the men came to Jesus, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to ask, ‘Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?’”
units.rightText: And when the men were come unto him, they said, John the Baptist hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he that cometh, or look we for another?

units.leftText: At that very hour Jesus healed many people of their diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and He gave sight to many who were blind.
units.rightText: In that hour he cured many of diseases and plagues and evil spirits; and on many that were blind he bestowed sight.

units.leftText: So He replied, “Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
units.rightText: And he answered and said unto them, Go and tell John the things which ye have seen and heard; the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, the poor have good tidings preached to them.
leftNotes: 7:22 A leper was one afflicted with a skin disease. See Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me. ” Jesus Testifies about John (Malachi 3:1–5|MAL 3:1-5*; Matthew 11:7–19|MAT 11:7-19*)
units.rightText: And blessed is he, whosoever shall find no occasion of stumbling in me.
leftNotes: 7:23 Or who is not offended by Me

units.leftText: After John’s messengers had left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?
units.rightText: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to behold? a reed shaken with the wind?

units.leftText: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces.
units.rightText: But what went ye out to see? a man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they that are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in kings’ courts.

units.leftText: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
units.rightText: But what went ye out to see? a prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.

units.leftText: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’
units.rightText: This is he of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, Who shall prepare thy way before thee.
leftNotes: 7:27 Malachi 3:1|MAL 3:1*

units.leftText: I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John, yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
units.rightText: I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there is none greater than John: yet he that is but little in the kingdom of God is greater than he.

units.leftText: All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, acknowledged God’s justice. For they had received the baptism of John.
units.rightText: And all the people when they heard, and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.

units.leftText: But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected God’s purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by John.
units.rightText: But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected for themselves the counsel of God, being not baptized of him.

units.leftText: “To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?
units.rightText: Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation, and to what are they like?

units.leftText: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’
units.rightText: They are like unto children that sit in the marketplace, and call one to another; who say, We piped unto you, and ye did not dance; we wailed, and ye did not weep.

units.leftText: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon!’
units.rightText: For John the Baptist is come eating no bread nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a demon.

units.leftText: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
units.rightText: The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold, a gluttonous man, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners!

units.leftText: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.” A Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus (Matthew 26:6–13|MAT 26:6-13*; Mark 14:3–9|MRK 14:3-9*; John 12:1–8|JHN 12:1-8*)
units.rightText: And wisdom is justified of all her children.

units.leftText: Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him, and He entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.
units.rightText: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he entered into the Pharisee’s house, and sat down to meat.

units.leftText: When a sinful woman from that town learned that Jesus was dining there, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
units.rightText: And behold, a woman who was in the city, a sinner; and when she knew that he was sitting at meat in the Pharisee’s house, she brought an alabaster cruse of ointment,

units.leftText: As she stood behind Him at His feet weeping, she began to wet His feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair. Then she kissed His feet and anointed them with the perfume.
units.rightText: and standing behind at his feet, weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.

units.leftText: When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him — for she is a sinner!”
units.rightText: Now when the Pharisee that had bidden him saw it, he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have perceived who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him, that she is a sinner.

units.leftText: But Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” “Tell me, Teacher,” he said.
units.rightText: And Jesus answering said unto him, Simon, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And he saith, Teacher, say on.

units.leftText: “Two men were debtors to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
units.rightText: A certain lender had two debtors: the one owed five hundred shillings, and the other fifty.
leftNotes: 7:41 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: When they were unable to repay him, he forgave both of them. Which one, then, will love him more?”
units.rightText: When they had not wherewith to pay, he forgave them both. Which of them therefore will love him most?

units.leftText: “I suppose the one who was forgiven more,” Simon replied. “You have judged correctly,” Jesus said.
units.rightText: Simon answered and said, He, I suppose, to whom he forgave the most. And he said unto him, Thou hast rightly judged.

units.leftText: And turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? When I entered your house, you did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
units.rightText: And turning to the woman, he said unto Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entered into thy house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath wetted my feet with her tears, and wiped them with her hair.

units.leftText: You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.
units.rightText: Thou gavest me no kiss: but she, since the time I came in, hath not ceased to kiss my feet.

units.leftText: You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume.
units.rightText: My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but she hath anointed my feet with ointment.

units.leftText: Therefore I tell you, her many sins have been forgiven, for she has loved much. But he who has been forgiven little loves little.”
units.rightText: Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
units.rightText: And he said unto her, Thy sins are forgiven.

units.leftText: But those at the table began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
units.rightText: And they that sat at meat with him began to say within themselves, Who is this that even forgiveth sins?

units.leftText: And Jesus told the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
units.rightText: And he said unto the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.

units.leftText: Soon afterward, Jesus traveled from one town and village to another, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with Him,
units.rightText: And it came to pass soon afterwards, that he went about through cities and villages, preaching and bringing the good tidings of the kingdom of God, and with him the twelve,

units.leftText: as well as some women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
units.rightText: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary that was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,

units.leftText: Joanna the wife of Herod’s household manager Chuza, Susanna, and many others. These women were ministering to them out of their own means. The Parable of the Sower (Matthew 13:1–23|MAT 13:1-23*; Mark 4:1–20|MRK 4:1-20*)
units.rightText: and Joanna the wife of Chuzas Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others, who ministered unto them of their substance.
leftNotes: 8:3 TR to Him

units.leftText: While a large crowd was gathering and people were coming to Jesus from town after town, He told them this parable:
units.rightText: And when a great multitude came together, and they of every city resorted unto him, he spake by a parable:

units.leftText: “A farmer went out to sow his seed. And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, where it was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it.
units.rightText: The sower went forth to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden under foot, and the birds of the heaven devoured it.

units.leftText: Some fell on rocky ground, and when it came up, the seedlings withered because they had no moisture.
units.rightText: And other fell on the rock; and as soon as it grew, it withered away, because it had no moisture.

units.leftText: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up with it and choked the seedlings.
units.rightText: And other fell amidst the thorns; and the thorns grew with it, and choked it.

units.leftText: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprang up and produced a crop — a hundredfold.” As Jesus said this, He called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
units.rightText: And other fell into the good ground, and grew, and brought forth fruit a hundredfold. As he said these things, he cried, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

units.leftText: Then His disciples asked Him what this parable meant.
units.rightText: And his disciples asked him what this parable might be.

units.leftText: He replied, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to others I speak in parables, so that, ‘though seeing, they may not see; though hearing, they may not understand.’
units.rightText: And he said, Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God: but to the rest in parables; that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.
leftNotes: 8:10 Isaiah 6:9|ISA 6:9* (See also LXX)

units.leftText: Now this is the meaning of the parable: The seed is the word of God.
units.rightText: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.

units.leftText: The seeds along the path are those who hear, but the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
units.rightText: And those by the way side are they that have heard; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word from their heart, that they may not believe and be saved.
leftNotes: 8:12 Literally the ones; also in verses 13, 14, and 15

units.leftText: The seeds on rocky ground are those who hear the word and receive it with joy, but they have no root. They believe for a season, but in the time of testing, they fall away.
units.rightText: And those on the rock are they who, when they have heard, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, who for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.

units.leftText: The seeds that fell among the thorns are those who hear, but as they go on their way, they are choked by the worries, riches, and pleasures of this life, and their fruit does not mature.
units.rightText: And that which fell among the thorns, these are they that have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection.

units.leftText: But the seeds on good soil are those with a noble and good heart, who hear the word, cling to it, and by persevering produce a crop. The Lesson of the Lamp (Mark 4:21–25|MRK 4:21-25*)
units.rightText: And that in the good ground, these are such as in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, hold it fast, and bring forth fruit with patience.

units.leftText: No one lights a lamp and covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.
units.rightText: And no man, when he hath lighted a lamp, covereth it with a vessel, or putteth it under a bed; but putteth it on a stand, that they that enter in may see the light.

units.leftText: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be made known and brought to light.
units.rightText: For nothing is hid, that shall not be made manifest; nor anything secret, that shall not be known and come to light.

units.leftText: Pay attention, therefore, to how you listen. Whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.” Jesus’ Mother and Brothers (Matthew 12:46–50|MAT 12:46-50*; Mark 3:31–35|MRK 3:31-35*)
units.rightText: Take heed therefore how ye hear: for whosoever hath, to him shall be given; and whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that which he thinketh he hath.

units.leftText: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came to see Him, but they were unable to reach Him because of the crowd.
units.rightText: And there came to him his mother and brethren, and they could not come at him for the crowd.

units.leftText: He was told, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see You.”
units.rightText: And it was told him, Thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to see thee.

units.leftText: But He replied, “My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out.” Jesus Calms the Storm (Psalm 107:1–43|PSA 107:1-43*; Matthew 8:23–27|MAT 8:23-27*; Mark 4:35–41|MRK 4:35-41*)
units.rightText: But he answered and said unto them, My mother and my brethren are these that hear the word of God, and do it.

units.leftText: One day Jesus said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” So He got into a boat with them and set out.
units.rightText: Now it came to pass on one of those days, that he entered into a boat, himself and his disciples; and he said unto them, Let us go over unto the other side of the lake: and they launched forth.

units.leftText: As they sailed, He fell asleep, and a windstorm came down on the lake, so that the boat was being swamped, and they were in great danger.
units.rightText: But as they sailed he fell asleep: and there came down a storm of wind on the lake; and they were filling with water, and were in jeopardy.

units.leftText: The disciples went and woke Him, saying, “Master, Master, we are perishing!”
units.rightText: And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we perish. And he awoke, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water: and they ceased, and there was a calm.

units.leftText: “Where is your faith?” He asked. Frightened and amazed, they asked one another, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!” The Demons and the Pigs (Matthew 8:28–34|MAT 8:28-34*; Mark 5:1–20|MRK 5:1-20*)
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Where is your faith? And being afraid they marvelled, saying one to another, Who then is this, that he commandeth even the winds and the water, and they obey him?

units.leftText: Then they sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, across the lake from Galilee.
units.rightText: And they arrived at the country of the Gerasenes, which is over against Galilee.
leftNotes: 8:26 BYZ and TR Gadarenes; Tischendorf Gergesenes; also in verse 37

units.leftText: When Jesus stepped ashore, He was met by a demon-possessed man from the town. For a long time this man had not worn clothing or lived in a house, but he stayed in the tombs.
units.rightText: And when he was come forth upon the land, there met him a certain man out of the city, who had demons; and for a long time he had worn no clothes, and abode not in any house, but in the tombs.

units.leftText: When the man saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before Him, shouting in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You not to torture me!”
units.rightText: And when he saw Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the Most High God? I beseech thee, torment me not.

units.leftText: For Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him, and though he was bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and been driven by the demon into solitary places.
units.rightText: For he was commanding the unclean spirit to come out from the man. For oftentimes it had seized him: and he was kept under guard, and bound with chains and fetters; and breaking the bands asunder, he was driven of the demon into the deserts.

units.leftText: “What is your name?” Jesus asked.
units.rightText: And Jesus asked him, What is thy name? And he said, Legion; for many demons were entered into him.

units.leftText: And the demons kept begging Jesus not to order them to go into the Abyss.
units.rightText: And they entreated him that he would not command them to depart into the abyss.

units.leftText: There on the hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding. So the demons begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs, and He gave them permission.
units.rightText: Now there was there a herd of many swine feeding on the mountain: and they entreated him that he would give them leave to enter into them. And he gave them leave.

units.leftText: Then the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.
units.rightText: And the demons came out from the man, and entered into the swine: and the herd rushed down the steep into the lake, and were drowned.

units.leftText: When those tending the pigs saw what had happened, they ran off and reported this in the town and countryside.
units.rightText: And when they that fed them saw what had come to pass, they fled, and told it in the city and in the country.

units.leftText: So the people went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man whom the demons had left, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
units.rightText: And they went out to see what had come to pass; and they came to Jesus, and found the man, from whom the demons were gone out, sitting, clothed and in his right mind, at the feet of Jesus: and they were afraid.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, those who had seen it reported how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
units.rightText: And they that saw it told them how he that was possessed with demons was made whole.

units.leftText: Then all the people of the region of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them. So He got into the boat and started back.
units.rightText: And all the people of the country of the Gerasenes round about asked him to depart from them; for they were holden with great fear: and he entered into a boat, and returned.

units.leftText: The man whom the demons had left begged to go with Jesus. But He sent him away, saying,
units.rightText: But the man from whom the demons were gone out prayed him that he might be with him: but he sent him away, saying,

units.leftText: “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” So the man went away and proclaimed all over the town how much Jesus had done for him. The Healing Touch of Jesus (Matthew 9:18–26|MAT 9:18-26*; Mark 5:21–43|MRK 5:21-43*)
units.rightText: Return to thy house, and declare how great things God hath done for thee. And he went his way, publishing throughout the whole city how great things Jesus had done for him.

units.leftText: When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed Him, for they had all been waiting for Him.
