units.rightText: And as Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed him; for they were all waiting for him.

units.leftText: Just then a synagogue leader named Jairus came and fell at Jesus’ feet. He begged Him to come to his house,
units.rightText: And behold, there came a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue: and he fell down at Jesus’ feet, and besought him to come into his house;

units.leftText: because his only daughter, who was about twelve, was dying.
units.rightText: for he had an only daughter, about twelve years of age, and she was dying. But as he went the multitudes thronged him.

units.leftText: including a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all her money on physicians, but no one was able to heal her.
units.rightText: And a woman having an issue of blood twelve years, who had spent all her living upon physicians, and could not be healed of any,
leftNotes: 8:43 NE and WH do not include She had spent all her money on physicians.

units.leftText: She came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of His cloak, and immediately her bleeding stopped.
units.rightText: came behind him, and touched the border of his garment: and immediately the issue of her blood stanched.

units.leftText: “Who touched Me?” Jesus asked. But they all denied it. “Master,” said Peter, “the people are crowding and pressing against You.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said, Who is it that touched me? And when all denied, Peter said, and they that were with him, Master, the multitudes press thee and crush thee.
leftNotes: 8:45 BYZ and TR include and those who were with him.

units.leftText: But Jesus declared, “Someone touched Me, for I know that power has gone out from Me.”
units.rightText: But Jesus said, Some one did touch me; for I perceived that power had gone forth from me.

units.leftText: Then the woman, seeing that she could not escape notice, came trembling and fell down before Him. In the presence of all the people, she explained why she had touched Him and how she had immediately been healed.
units.rightText: And when the woman saw that she was not hid, she came trembling, and falling down before him declared in the presence of all the people for what cause she touched him, and how she was healed immediately.

units.leftText: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace.”
units.rightText: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.

units.leftText: While He was still speaking, someone arrived from the house of the synagogue leader. “Your daughter is dead,” he told Jairus. “Do not bother the Teacher anymore.”
units.rightText: While he yet spake, there cometh one from the ruler of the synagogue’s house, saying, Thy daughter is dead; trouble not the Teacher.

units.leftText: But Jesus overheard them and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed.”
units.rightText: But Jesus hearing it, answered him, Fear not: only believe, and she shall be made whole.

units.leftText: When He entered the house, He did not allow anyone to go in with Him except Peter, John, James, and the child’s father and mother.
units.rightText: And when he came to the house, he suffered not any man to enter in with him, save Peter, and John, and James, and the father of the maiden and her mother.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But Jesus said, “Stop weeping; she is not dead but asleep.”
units.rightText: And all were weeping, and bewailing her: but he said, Weep not; for she is not dead, but sleepeth.

units.leftText: And they laughed at Him, knowing that she was dead.
units.rightText: And they laughed him to scorn, knowing that she was dead.

units.leftText: But Jesus took her by the hand and called out, “Child, get up!”
units.rightText: But he, taking her by the hand, called, saying, Maiden, arise.

units.leftText: Her spirit returned, and at once she got up. And He directed that she be given something to eat.
units.rightText: And her spirit returned, and she rose up immediately: and he commanded that something be given her to eat.

units.leftText: Her parents were astounded, but Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.
units.rightText: And her parents were amazed: but he charged them to tell no man what had been done.

units.leftText: Then Jesus called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and power to cure diseases.
units.rightText: And he called the twelve together, and gave them power and authority over all demons, and to cure diseases.
leftNotes: 9:1 TR His twelve disciples

units.leftText: And He sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
units.rightText: And he sent them forth to preach the kingdom of God, and to heal the sick.

units.leftText: “Take nothing for the journey,” He told them, “no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, no second tunic.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staff, nor wallet, nor bread, nor money; neither have two coats.
leftNotes: 9:3 Or silver coins

units.leftText: Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that area.
units.rightText: And into whatsoever house ye enter, there abide, and thence depart.

units.leftText: If anyone does not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town, as a testimony against them.”
units.rightText: And as many as receive you not, when ye depart from that city, shake off the dust from your feet for a testimony against them.

units.leftText: So they set out and went from village to village, preaching the gospel and healing people everywhere. Herod Tries to See Jesus (Matthew 14:1–12|MAT 14:1-12*; Mark 6:14–29|MRK 6:14-29*)
units.rightText: And they departed, and went throughout the villages, preaching the gospel, and healing everywhere.

units.leftText: When Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, he was perplexed. For some were saying that John had risen from the dead,
units.rightText: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done: and he was much perplexed, because that it was said by some, that John was risen from the dead;

units.leftText: others that Elijah had appeared, and still others that a prophet of old had arisen.
units.rightText: and by some, that Elijah had appeared; and by others, that one of the old prophets was risen again.

units.leftText: “I beheaded John,” Herod said, “but who is this man I hear such things about?” And he kept trying to see Jesus. The Feeding of the Five Thousand (Matthew 14:13–21|MAT 14:13-21*; Mark 6:30–44|MRK 6:30-44*; John 6:1–15|JHN 6:1-15*)
units.rightText: And Herod said, John I beheaded: but who is this, about whom I hear such things? And he sought to see him.

units.leftText: Then the apostles returned and reported to Jesus all that they had done. Taking them away privately, He withdrew to a town called Bethsaida.
units.rightText: And the apostles, when they were returned, declared unto him what things they had done. And he took them, and withdrew apart to a city called Bethsaida.

units.leftText: But the crowds found out and followed Him. He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and He healed those who needed healing.
units.rightText: But the multitudes perceiving it followed him: and he welcomed them, and spake to them of the kingdom of God, and them that had need of healing he cured.

units.leftText: As the day neared its end, the Twelve came to Jesus and said, “Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding villages and countryside for lodging and provisions. For we are in a desolate place here.”
units.rightText: And the day began to wear away; and the twelve came, and said unto him, Send the multitude away, that they may go into the villages and country round about, and lodge, and get provisions: for we are here in a desert place.

units.leftText: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.”
units.rightText: But he said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they said, We have no more than five loaves and two fishes; except we should go and buy food for all this people.

units.leftText: (There were about five thousand men.)
units.rightText: For they were about five thousand men. And he said unto his disciples, Make them sit down in companies, about fifty each.

units.leftText: They did so, and everyone was seated.
units.rightText: And they did so, and made them all sit down.

units.leftText: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke them. Then He gave them to the disciples to set before the people.
units.rightText: And he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed them, and brake; and gave to the disciples to set before the multitude.

units.leftText: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over. Peter’s Confession of Christ (Matthew 16:13–20|MAT 16:13-20*; Mark 8:27–30|MRK 8:27-30*; John 6:67–71|JHN 6:67-71*)
units.rightText: And they ate, and were all filled: and there was taken up that which remained over to them of broken pieces, twelve baskets.

units.leftText: One day as Jesus was praying in private and the disciples were with Him, He questioned them: “Who do the crowds say I am?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as he was praying apart, the disciples were with him: and he asked them, saying, Who do the multitudes say that I am?

units.leftText: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, that a prophet of old has arisen.”
units.rightText: And they answering said, John the Baptist; but others say, Elijah; and others, that one of the old prophets is risen again.

units.leftText: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “The Christ of God.” Christ’s Passion Foretold (Matthew 16:21–23|MAT 16:21-23*; Mark 8:31–33|MRK 8:31-33*)
units.rightText: And he said unto them, But who say ye that I am? And Peter answering said, The Christ of God.

units.leftText: Jesus strictly warned them not to tell this to anyone.
units.rightText: But he charged them, and commanded them to tell this to no man;

units.leftText: “The Son of Man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.” Take Up Your Cross (Matthew 16:24–28|MAT 16:24-28*; Mark 8:34–38|MRK 8:34-38*)
units.rightText: saying, The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and the third day be raised up.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to all of them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.
units.rightText: And he said unto all, If any man would come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.

units.leftText: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will save it.
units.rightText: For whosoever would save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it.

units.leftText: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or forfeit his very self?
units.rightText: For what is a man profited, if he gain the whole world, and lose or forfeit his own self?

units.leftText: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when He comes in His glory and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
units.rightText: For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in his own glory, and the glory of the Father, and of the holy angels.

units.leftText: But I tell you truly, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God.” The Transfiguration (Matthew 17:1–13|MAT 17:1-13*; Mark 9:1–13|MRK 9:1-13*; 2 Peter 1:16–21|2PE 1:16-21*)
units.rightText: But I tell you of a truth, There are some of them that stand here, who shall in no wise taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: About eight days after Jesus had said these things, He took with Him Peter, John, and James, and went up on a mountain to pray.
units.rightText: And it came to pass about eight days after these sayings, that he took with him Peter and John and James, and went up into the mountain to pray.

units.leftText: And as He was praying, the appearance of His face changed, and His clothes became radiantly white.
units.rightText: And as he was praying, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment became white and dazzling.

units.leftText: Suddenly two men, Moses and Elijah, began talking with Jesus.
units.rightText: And behold, there talked with him two men, who were Moses and Elijah;

units.leftText: They appeared in glory and spoke about His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
units.rightText: who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Meanwhile Peter and his companions were overcome by sleep, but when they awoke, they saw Jesus’ glory and the two men standing with Him.
units.rightText: Now Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep: but when they were fully awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.

units.leftText: As Moses and Elijah were leaving, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters — one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” ( He did not know what he was saying.)
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as they were parting from him, Peter said unto Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah: not knowing what he said.
leftNotes: 9:33 Or three tabernacles

units.leftText: While Peter was speaking, a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
units.rightText: And while he said these things, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud.

units.leftText: And a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!”
units.rightText: And a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my Son, my chosen: hear ye him.
leftNotes: 9:35 BYZ and TR This is My beloved Son; see Matthew 17:5|MAT 17:5*.

units.leftText: After the voice had spoken, only Jesus was present with them. The disciples kept this to themselves, and in those days they did not tell anyone what they had seen. The Boy with an Evil Spirit (Matthew 17:14–18|MAT 17:14-18*; Mark 9:14–29|MRK 9:14-29*)
units.rightText: And when the voice came, Jesus was found alone. And they held their peace, and told no man in those days any of the things which they had seen.

units.leftText: The next day, when they came down from the mountain, Jesus was met by a large crowd.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, on the next day, when they were come down from the mountain, a great multitude met him.

units.leftText: Suddenly a man in the crowd cried out, “Teacher, I beg You to look at my son, for he is my only child.
units.rightText: And behold, a man from the multitude cried, saying, Teacher, I beseech thee to look upon my son; for he is mine only child:

units.leftText: A spirit keeps seizing him, and he screams abruptly. It throws him into convulsions so that he foams at the mouth. It keeps mauling him and rarely departs from him.
units.rightText: and behold, a spirit taketh him, and he suddenly crieth out; and it teareth him that he foameth, and it hardly departeth from him, bruising him sorely.

units.leftText: I begged Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable.”
units.rightText: And I besought thy disciples to cast it out; and they could not.

units.leftText: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you and put up with you? Bring your son here.”
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you, and bear with you? bring hither thy son.

units.leftText: Even while the boy was approaching, the demon slammed him to the ground in a convulsion. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father. The Second Prediction of the Passion (Matthew 17:22–23|MAT 17:22-23*; Mark 9:30–32|MRK 9:30-32*)
units.rightText: And as he was yet a coming, the demon dashed him down, and tare him grievously. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.

units.leftText: And they were all astonished at the greatness of God.
units.rightText: And they were all astonished at the majesty of God. But while all were marvelling at all the things which he did, he said unto his disciples,

units.leftText: “Let these words sink into your ears: The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.”
units.rightText: Let these words sink into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered up into the hands of men.

units.leftText: But they did not understand this statement. It was veiled from them so that they could not comprehend it, and they were afraid to ask Him about it. The Greatest in the Kingdom (Matthew 18:1–5|MAT 18:1-5*; Mark 9:33–41|MRK 9:33-41*)
units.rightText: But they understood not this saying, and it was concealed from them, that they should not perceive it; and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.

units.leftText: Then an argument started among the disciples as to which of them would be the greatest.
units.rightText: And there arose a reasoning among them, which of them was the greatest.

units.leftText: But Jesus, knowing the thoughts of their hearts, had a little child stand beside Him.
units.rightText: But when Jesus saw the reasoning of their heart, he took a little child, and set him by his side,

units.leftText: And He said to them, “Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me. For whoever is the least among all of you, he is the greatest.”
units.rightText: and said unto them, Whosoever shall receive this little child in my name receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me receiveth him that sent me: for he that is least among you all, the same is great.

units.leftText: “Master,” said John, “we saw someone driving out demons in Your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not accompany us.”
units.rightText: And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out demons in thy name; and we forbade him, because he followeth not with us.

units.leftText: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replied, “for whoever is not against you is for you.” The Samaritans Reject Jesus
units.rightText: But Jesus said unto him, Forbid him not: for he that is not against you is for you.

units.leftText: As the day of His ascension approached, Jesus resolutely set out for Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the days were well-nigh come that he should be received up, he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem,

units.leftText: He sent messengers on ahead, who went into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for Him.
units.rightText: and sent messengers before his face: and they went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, to make ready for him.

units.leftText: But the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And they did not receive him, because his face was as though he were going to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: When the disciples James and John saw this, they asked, “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?”
units.rightText: And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we bid fire to come down from heaven, and consume them?
leftNotes: 9:54 BYZ and TR from heaven, just as Elijah did; see 2 Kings 1:10–12|2KI 1:10-12*.

units.leftText: But Jesus turned and rebuked them.
units.rightText: But he turned, and rebuked them.
leftNotes: 9:55 BYZ and TR include and He said, “You do not know what kind of spirit you are of. 56*For the Son of Man did not come to destroy the lives of men, but to save them.”

units.leftText: And He and His disciples went on to another village. The Cost of Discipleship (Matthew 8:18–22|MAT 8:18-22*; Luke 14:25–33|LUK 14:25-33*; John 6:59–66|JHN 6:59-66*)
units.rightText: And they went to another village.

units.leftText: As they were walking along the road, someone said to Jesus, “I will follow You wherever You go.”
units.rightText: And as they went on the way, a certain man said unto him, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the heaven have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.

units.leftText: Then He said to another man, “Follow Me.” The man replied, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
units.rightText: And he said unto another, Follow me. But he said, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.

units.leftText: But Jesus told him, “Let the dead bury their own dead. You, however, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”
units.rightText: But he said unto him, Leave the dead to bury their own dead; but go thou and publish abroad the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: Still another said, “I will follow You, Lord; but first let me bid farewell to my family.”
units.rightText: And another also said, I will follow thee, Lord; but first suffer me to bid farewell to them that are at my house.

units.leftText: Then Jesus declared, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
units.rightText: But Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plow, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: After this, the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of Him to every town and place He was about to visit.
units.rightText: Now after these things the Lord appointed seventy others, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself was about to come.
leftNotes: 10:1 NE, BYZ, and TR seventy; also in verse 17

units.leftText: And He told them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, The harvest indeed is plenteous, but the laborers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he send forth laborers into his harvest.

units.leftText: Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
units.rightText: Go your ways; behold, I send you forth as lambs in the midst of wolves.

units.leftText: Carry no purse or bag or sandals. Do not greet anyone along the road.
units.rightText: Carry no purse, no wallet, no shoes; and salute no man on the way.

units.leftText: Whatever house you enter, begin by saying, ‘Peace to this house.’
units.rightText: And into whatsoever house ye shall enter, first say, Peace be to this house.

units.leftText: If a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.
units.rightText: And if a son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon him: but if not, it shall turn to you again.

units.leftText: Stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered. For the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not move around from house to house.
units.rightText: And in that same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the laborer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.
leftNotes: 10:7 See Leviticus 19:13|LEV 19:13* and Deuteronomy 24:14–15; cited in 1 Timothy 5:18.

units.leftText: If you enter a town and they welcome you, eat whatever is set before you.
units.rightText: And into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you, eat such things as are set before you:

units.leftText: Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God is near you.’
units.rightText: and heal the sick that are therein, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.

units.leftText: But if you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go into the streets and declare,
units.rightText: But into whatsoever city ye shall enter, and they receive you not, go out into the streets thereof and say,

units.leftText: ‘Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you. Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is near.’
units.rightText: Even the dust from your city, that cleaveth to our feet, we wipe off against you: nevertheless know this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh.

units.leftText: I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town. Woe to the Unrepentant (Matthew 11:20–24|MAT 11:20-24*)
units.rightText: I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom, than for that city.

units.leftText: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
units.rightText: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which were done in you, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

units.leftText: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
units.rightText: But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment, than for you.

units.leftText: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!
units.rightText: And thou, Capernaum, shalt thou be exalted unto heaven? thou shalt be brought down unto Hades.

units.leftText: Whoever listens to you listens to Me; whoever rejects you rejects Me; and whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me.” The Joyful Return
units.rightText: He that heareth you heareth me; and he that rejecteth you rejecteth me; and he that rejecteth me rejecteth him that sent me.

units.leftText: The seventy-two returned with joy and said, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.”
units.rightText: And the seventy returned with joy, saying, Lord, even the demons are subject unto us in thy name.

units.leftText: So He told them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, I beheld Satan fallen as lightning from heaven.

units.leftText: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will harm you.
units.rightText: Behold, I have given you authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall in any wise hurt you.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.” Jesus’ Prayer of Thanksgiving (Matthew 11:25–30|MAT 11:25-30*)
units.rightText: Nevertheless in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.

units.leftText: At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.
units.rightText: In that same hour he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou didst hide these things from the wise and understanding, and didst reveal them unto babes: yea, Father; for so it was well-pleasing in thy sight.

units.leftText: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.”
units.rightText: All things have been delivered unto me of my Father: and no one knoweth who the Son is, save the Father; and who the Father is, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son willeth to reveal him.

units.leftText: Then Jesus turned to the disciples and said privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
units.rightText: And turning to the disciples, he said privately, Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see:

units.leftText: For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.” The Parable of the Good Samaritan
units.rightText: for I say unto you, that many prophets and kings desired to see the things which ye see, and saw them not; and to hear the things which ye hear, and heard them not.

units.leftText: One day an expert in the law stood up to test Him. “Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
units.rightText: And behold, a certain lawyer stood up and made trial of him, saying, Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?

units.leftText: “What is written in the Law?” Jesus replied. “How do you read it?”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou?

units.leftText: He answered, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’ and ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”
units.rightText: And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbor as thyself.
leftNotes: 10:27 Deuteronomy 6:5|DEU 6:5*
10:27 Leviticus 19:18|LEV 19:18*

units.leftText: “You have answered correctly,” Jesus said. “Do this and you will live.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.

units.leftText: But wanting to justify himself, he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
units.rightText: But he, desiring to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbor?

units.leftText: Jesus took up this question and said, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.
units.rightText: Jesus made answer and said, A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho; and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead.

units.leftText: Now by chance a priest was going down the same road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
units.rightText: And by chance a certain priest was going down that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

units.leftText: So too, when a Levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side.
units.rightText: And in like manner a Levite also, when he came to the place, and saw him, passed by on the other side.

units.leftText: But a Samaritan on a journey came upon him, and when he saw him, he had compassion.
units.rightText: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he was moved with compassion,

units.leftText: He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
units.rightText: and came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on them oil and wine; and he set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

units.leftText: The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper. ‘Take care of him,’ he said, ‘and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.’
units.rightText: And on the morrow he took out two shillings, and gave them to the host, and said, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, I, when I come back again, will repay thee.
leftNotes: 10:35 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”
units.rightText: Which of these three, thinkest thou, proved neighbor unto him that fell among the robbers?

units.leftText: “The one who showed him mercy,” replied the expert in the law. Then Jesus told him, “Go and do likewise.” Martha and Mary
units.rightText: And he said, He that showed mercy on him. And Jesus said unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.

units.leftText: As they traveled along, Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.
units.rightText: Now as they went on their way, he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.

units.leftText: She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message.
units.rightText: And she had a sister called Mary, who also sat at the Lord’s feet, and heard his word.

units.leftText: But Martha was distracted by all the preparations to be made. She came to Jesus and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me!”
units.rightText: But Martha was cumbered about much serving; and she came up to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister did leave me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.

units.leftText: “Martha, Martha,” the Lord replied, “you are worried and upset about many things.
units.rightText: But the Lord answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art anxious and troubled about many things:

units.leftText: But only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”
units.rightText: but one thing is needful: for Mary hath chosen the good part, which shall not be taken away from her.

units.leftText: One day in a place where Jesus had just finished praying, one of His disciples requested, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as he was praying in a certain place, that when he ceased, one of his disciples said unto him, Lord, teach us to pray, even as John also taught his disciples.

units.leftText: So Jesus told them, “When you pray, say: ‘Father, hallowed be Your name. Your kingdom come.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, When ye pray, say, Father, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come.
leftNotes: 11:2 BYZ and TR Our Father in heaven; see Matthew 6:9|MAT 6:9*.
11:2 BYZ and TR include Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven; see Matthew 6:10|MAT 6:10*.

units.leftText: Give us each day our daily bread.
units.rightText: Give us day by day our daily bread.

units.leftText: And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who sins against us. And lead us not into temptation. ’” Ask, Seek, Knock (Matthew 7:7–12|MAT 7:7-12*)
units.rightText: And forgive us our sins; for we ourselves also forgive every one that is indebted to us. And bring us not into temptation.
leftNotes: 11:4 BYZ and TR include but deliver us from the evil one; see Matthew 6:13|MAT 6:13*.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to them, “Suppose one of you goes to his friend at midnight and says, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go unto him at midnight, and say to him, Friend, lend me three loaves;

units.leftText: because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.’
units.rightText: for a friend of mine is come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him;

units.leftText: And suppose the one inside answers, ‘Do not bother me. My door is already shut, and my children and I are in bed. I cannot get up to give you anything.’
units.rightText: and he from within shall answer and say, Trouble me not: the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot rise and give thee?

units.leftText: I tell you, even though he will not get up to provide for him because of his friendship, yet because of the man’s persistence, he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
units.rightText: I say unto you, Though he will not rise and give him because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will arise and give him as many as he needeth.

units.leftText: So I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
units.rightText: And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.

units.leftText: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.
units.rightText: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

units.leftText: What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead?
units.rightText: And of which of you that is a father shall his son ask a loaf, and he give him a stone? or a fish, and he for a fish give him a serpent?
leftNotes: 11:11 BYZ and TR if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone, or for a fish; see Matthew 7:9–10|MAT 7:9-10*.

units.leftText: Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
units.rightText: Or if he shall ask an egg, will he give him a scorpion?

units.leftText: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!” A House Divided (Matthew 12:22–30|MAT 12:22-30*; Mark 3:20–27|MRK 3:20-27*)
units.rightText: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?

units.leftText: One day Jesus was driving out a demon that was mute. And when the demon was gone, the man who had been mute spoke. The crowds were amazed,
units.rightText: And he was casting out a demon that was dumb. And it came to pass, when the demon was gone out, the dumb man spake; and the multitudes marvelled.

units.leftText: but some of them said, “It is by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons, that He drives out demons.”
units.rightText: But some of them said, By Beelzebub the prince of the demons casteth he out demons.
leftNotes: 11:15 WH Beezeboul; Vulgate Beelzebub; also in verses 18 and 19

units.leftText: And others tested Him by demanding a sign from heaven.
units.rightText: And others, trying him, sought of him a sign from heaven.

units.leftText: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall.
units.rightText: But he, knowing their thoughts, said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and a house divided against a house falleth.

units.leftText: If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? After all, you say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.
units.rightText: And if Satan also is divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? because ye say that I cast out demons by Beelzebub.

units.leftText: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.
units.rightText: And if I by Beelzebub cast out demons, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges.

units.leftText: But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
units.rightText: But if I by the finger of God cast out demons, then is the kingdom of God come upon you.

units.leftText: When a strong man, fully armed, guards his house, his possessions are secure.
units.rightText: When the strong man fully armed guardeth his own court, his goods are in peace:

units.leftText: But when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, he takes away the armor in which the man trusted, and then he divides up his plunder.
units.rightText: but when a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he taketh from him his whole armor wherein he trusted, and divideth his spoils.

units.leftText: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters. An Unclean Spirit Returns (Matthew 12:43–45|MAT 12:43-45*)
units.rightText: He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.

units.leftText: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’
units.rightText: The unclean spirit when he is gone out of the man, passeth through waterless places, seeking rest, and finding none, he saith, I will turn back unto my house whence I came out.

units.leftText: On its return, it finds the house swept clean and put in order.
units.rightText: And when he is come, he findeth it swept and garnished.

units.leftText: Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there. And the final plight of that man is worse than the first.” True Blessedness
units.rightText: Then goeth he, and taketh to him seven other spirits more evil than himself; and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man becometh worse than the first.

units.leftText: As Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said, “Blessed is the womb that bore You, and blessed are the breasts that nursed You!”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice, and said unto him, Blessed is the womb that bare thee, and the breasts which thou didst suck.

units.leftText: But He replied, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.” The Sign of Jonah (Jonah 3:1–10|JON 3:1-10*; Matthew 12:38–42|MAT 12:38-42*)
units.rightText: But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.

units.leftText: As the crowds were increasing, Jesus said, “This is a wicked generation. It demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.
units.rightText: And when the multitudes were gathering together unto him, he began to say, This generation is an evil generation: it seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it but the sign of Jonah.

units.leftText: For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.
units.rightText: For even as Jonah became a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.

units.leftText: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.
units.rightText: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and shall condemn them: for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

units.leftText: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here. The Lamp of the Body (Matthew 6:22–24|MAT 6:22-24*)
units.rightText: The men of Nineveh shall stand up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, a greater than Jonah is here.

units.leftText: No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.
units.rightText: No man, when he hath lighted a lamp, putteth it in a cellar, neither under the bushel, but on the stand, that they which enter in may see the light.

units.leftText: Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light. But when they are bad, your body is full of darkness.
units.rightText: The lamp of thy body is thine eye: when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when it is evil, thy body also is full of darkness.
leftNotes: 11:34 Literally When your eye is sound; see Proverbs 22:9|PRO 22:9*.
11:34 Literally when it is evil; see Proverbs 23:6|PRO 23:6* and Proverbs 28:22.

units.leftText: Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness.
units.rightText: Look therefore whether the light that is in thee be not darkness.

units.leftText: So if your whole body is full of light, with no part of it in darkness, you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you.” Woes to Pharisees and Experts in the Law (Matthew 23:1–36|MAT 23:1-36*)
units.rightText: If therefore thy whole body be full of light, having no part dark, it shall be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its bright shining doth give thee light.

units.leftText: As Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee invited Him to dine with him; so He went in and reclined at the table.
units.rightText: Now as he spake, a Pharisee asketh him to dine with him: and he went in, and sat down to meat.

units.leftText: But the Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash before the meal.
units.rightText: And when the Pharisee saw it, he marvelled that he had not first bathed himself before dinner.

units.leftText: Then the Lord said, “Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.
units.rightText: And the Lord said unto him, Now ye the Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter; but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.

units.leftText: You fools! Did not the One who made the outside make the inside as well?
units.rightText: Ye foolish ones, did not he that made the outside make the inside also?

units.leftText: But give as alms the things that are within you, and behold, everything will be clean for you.
units.rightText: But give for alms those things which are within; and behold, all things are clean unto you.

units.leftText: Woe to you Pharisees! For you pay tithes of mint, rue, and every herb, but you disregard justice and the love of God. You should have practiced the latter without neglecting the former.
units.rightText: But woe unto you Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and every herb, and pass over justice and the love of God: but these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.

units.leftText: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
units.rightText: Woe unto you Pharisees! for ye love the chief seats in the synagogues, and the salutations in the marketplaces.

units.leftText: Woe to you! For you are like unmarked graves, which men walk over without even noticing.”
units.rightText: Woe unto you! for ye are as the tombs which appear not, and the men that walk over them know it not.

units.leftText: One of the experts in the law told Him, “Teacher, when You say these things, You insult us as well.”
units.rightText: And one of the lawyers answering saith unto him, Teacher, in saying this thou reproachest us also.

units.leftText: “Woe to you as well, experts in the law!” He replied. “For you weigh men down with heavy burdens, but you yourselves will not lift a finger to lighten their load.
units.rightText: And he said, Woe unto you lawyers also! for ye load men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.

units.leftText: Woe to you! For you build tombs for the prophets, but it was your fathers who killed them.
units.rightText: Woe unto you! for ye build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.

units.leftText: So you are witnesses consenting to the deeds of your fathers: They killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.
units.rightText: So ye are witnesses and consent unto the works of your fathers: for they killed them, and ye build their tombs.

units.leftText: Because of this, the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles; some of them they will kill and others they will persecute.’
units.rightText: Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send unto them prophets and apostles; and some of them they shall kill and persecute;

units.leftText: As a result, this generation will be charged with the blood of all the prophets that has been shed since the foundation of the world,
units.rightText: that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;

units.leftText: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, all of it will be charged to this generation.
units.rightText: from the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zachariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary: yea, I say unto you, it shall be required of this generation.
leftNotes: 11:51 Literally the house

units.leftText: Woe to you experts in the law! For you have taken away the key to knowledge. You yourselves have not entered, and you have hindered those who were entering.”
units.rightText: Woe unto you lawyers! for ye took away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.

units.leftText: As Jesus went on from there, the scribes and Pharisees began to oppose Him bitterly and to ply Him with questions about many things,
units.rightText: And when he was come out from thence, the scribes and the Pharisees began to press upon him vehemently, and to provoke him to speak of many things;

units.leftText: waiting to catch Him in something He might say.
units.rightText: laying wait for him, to catch something out of his mouth.

units.leftText: In the meantime, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another. Jesus began to speak first to His disciples: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
units.rightText: In the mean time, when the many thousands of the multitude were gathered together, insomuch that they trod one upon another, he began to say unto his disciples first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

units.leftText: There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
units.rightText: But there is nothing covered up, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.

units.leftText: What you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops. Fear God Alone (Matthew 10:26–31|MAT 10:26-31*)
units.rightText: Wherefore whatsoever ye have said in the darkness shall be heard in the light; and what ye have spoken in the ear in the inner chambers shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.

units.leftText: I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.
units.rightText: And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.

units.leftText: But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!
units.rightText: But I will warn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, who after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.
leftNotes: 12:5 Greek Gehenna

units.leftText: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.
units.rightText: Are not five sparrows sold for two pence? and not one of them is forgotten in the sight of God.
leftNotes: 12:6 Greek two assaria; an assarion was a Roman copper coin worth about 1/16 of a denarius.

units.leftText: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows. Confessing Christ (Matthew 10:32–33|MAT 10:32-33*)
units.rightText: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not: ye are of more value than many sparrows.

units.leftText: I tell you, everyone who confesses Me before men, the Son of Man will also confess him before the angels of God.
units.rightText: And I say unto you, Every one who shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of man also confess before the angels of God:

units.leftText: But whoever denies Me before men will be denied before the angels of God.
units.rightText: but he that denieth me in the presence of men shall be denied in the presence of the angels of God.

units.leftText: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
units.rightText: And every one who shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Spirit it shall not be forgiven.

units.leftText: When you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.
units.rightText: And when they bring you before the synagogues, and the rulers, and the authorities, be not anxious how or what ye shall answer, or what ye shall say:

units.leftText: For at that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say.” The Parable of the Rich Fool
units.rightText: for the Holy Spirit shall teach you in that very hour what ye ought to say.

units.leftText: Someone in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
units.rightText: And one out of the multitude said unto him, Teacher, bid my brother divide the inheritance with me.

units.leftText: But Jesus replied, “Man, who appointed Me judge or executor between you?”
units.rightText: But he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?

units.leftText: And He said to them, “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Take heed, and keep yourselves from all covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

units.leftText: Then He told them a parable: “The ground of a certain rich man produced an abundance.
units.rightText: And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully:

units.leftText: So he thought to himself, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?’
units.rightText: and he reasoned within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have not where to bestow my fruits?

units.leftText: Then he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, and there I will store up all my grain and my goods.
units.rightText: And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my grain and my goods.

units.leftText: Then I will say to myself, “You have plenty of good things laid up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and be merry!”’
units.rightText: And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, be merry.

units.leftText: But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life will be required of you. Then who will own what you have accumulated?’
units.rightText: But God said unto him, Thou foolish one, this night is thy soul required of thee; and the things which thou hast prepared, whose shall they be?

units.leftText: This is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.” Do Not Worry (Matthew 6:25–34|MAT 6:25-34*)
units.rightText: So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
units.rightText: And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Be not anxious for your life, what ye shall eat; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on.

units.leftText: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.
units.rightText: For the life is more than the food, and the body than the raiment.

units.leftText: Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!
units.rightText: Consider the ravens, that they sow not, neither reap; which have no store-chamber nor barn; and God feedeth them: of how much more value are ye than the birds!

units.leftText: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
units.rightText: And which of you by being anxious can add a cubit unto the measure of his life?
leftNotes: 12:25 Or a single cubit to his height; a cubit was approximately 18 inches or 45 centimeters.

units.leftText: So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?
units.rightText: If then ye are not able to do even that which is least, why are ye anxious concerning the rest?

units.leftText: Consider how the lilies grow: They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
units.rightText: Consider the lilies, how they grow: they toil not, neither do they spin; yet I say unto you, Even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
leftNotes: 12:27 NE and Tischendorf Consider the lilies: They do not spin or weave.

units.leftText: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith!
units.rightText: But if God doth so clothe the grass in the field, which to-day is, and to-morrow is cast into the oven; how much more shall he clothe you, O ye of little faith?

units.leftText: And do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about it.
units.rightText: And seek not ye what ye shall eat, and what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind.

units.leftText: For the Gentiles of the world strive after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
units.rightText: For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: but your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things.

units.leftText: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you. Treasures in Heaven (Matthew 6:19–21|MAT 6:19-21*)
units.rightText: Yet seek ye his kingdom, and these things shall be added unto you.
leftNotes: 12:31 BYZ and TR God’s; see Matthew 6:33|MAT 6:33*.

units.leftText: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
units.rightText: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.

units.leftText: Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Provide yourselves with purses that will not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
units.rightText: Sell that which ye have, and give alms; make for yourselves purses which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief draweth near, neither moth destroyeth.

units.leftText: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also. Readiness at Any Hour (Matthew 24:36–51|MAT 24:36-51*; Mark 13:32–37|MRK 13:32-37*)
units.rightText: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

units.leftText: Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.
units.rightText: Let your loins be girded about, and your lamps burning;

units.leftText: Then you will be like servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once.
units.rightText: and be ye yourselves like unto men looking for their lord, when he shall return from the marriage feast; that, when he cometh and knocketh, they may straightway open unto him.

units.leftText: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds on watch when he returns. Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve and will have them recline at the table, and he himself will come and wait on them.
units.rightText: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them sit down to meat, and shall come and serve them.

units.leftText: Even if he comes in the second or third watch of the night and finds them alert, those servants will be blessed.
units.rightText: And if he shall come in the second watch, and if in the third, and find them so, blessed are those servants.
leftNotes: 12:38 That is, between nine at night and three in the morning

units.leftText: But understand this: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
units.rightText: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched, and not have left his house to be broken through.
leftNotes: 12:39 BYZ and TR include he would have stayed awake, and

units.leftText: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.”
units.rightText: Be ye also ready: for in an hour that ye think not the Son of man cometh.

units.leftText: “Lord,” said Peter, “are You addressing this parable to us, or to everyone else as well?”
units.rightText: And Peter said, Lord, speakest thou this parable unto us, or even unto all?

units.leftText: And the Lord answered, “Who then is the faithful and wise manager, whom the master puts in charge of his servants to give them their portion at the proper time?
units.rightText: And the Lord said, Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall set over his household, to give them their portion of food in due season?

units.leftText: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.
units.rightText: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
units.rightText: Of a truth I say unto you, that he will set him over all that he hath.

units.leftText: But suppose that servant says in his heart, ‘My master will be a long time in coming,’ and he begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.
units.rightText: But if that servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken;

units.leftText: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate. Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the unbelievers.
units.rightText: the lord of that servant shall come in a day when he expecteth not, and in an hour when he knoweth not, and shall cut him asunder, and appoint his portion with the unfaithful.

units.leftText: That servant who knows his master’s will but does not get ready or follow his instructions will be beaten with many blows.
units.rightText: And that servant, who knew his lord’s will, and made not ready, nor did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes;

units.leftText: But the one who unknowingly does things worthy of punishment will be beaten with few blows. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required; and from him who has been entrusted with much, even more will be demanded. Not Peace but Division (Micah 7:1–6|MIC 7:1-6*; Matthew 10:34–39|MAT 10:34-39*)
units.rightText: but he that knew not, and did things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. And to whomsoever much is given, of him shall much be required: and to whom they commit much, of him will they ask the more.

units.leftText: I have come to ignite a fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
units.rightText: I came to cast fire upon the earth; and what do I desire, if it is already kindled?

units.leftText: But I have a baptism to undergo, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
units.rightText: But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished!

units.leftText: Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
units.rightText: Think ye that I am come to give peace in the earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:

units.leftText: From now on, five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.
units.rightText: for there shall be from henceforth five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.

units.leftText: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law. ” Interpreting the Present Time (Matthew 16:1–4|MAT 16:1-4*; Mark 8:11–13|MRK 8:11-13*)
units.rightText: They shall be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother in law against her daughter in law, and daughter in law against her mother in law.
leftNotes: 12:53 See Micah 7:6|MIC 7:6*.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to the crowds, “As soon as you see a cloud rising in the west, you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and that is what happens.
units.rightText: And he said to the multitudes also, When ye see a cloud rising in the west, straightway ye say, There cometh a shower; and so it cometh to pass.

units.leftText: And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It will be hot,’ and it is.
units.rightText: And when ye see a south wind blowing, ye say, There will be a scorching heat; and it cometh to pass.

units.leftText: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and sky. Why don’t you know how to interpret the present time? Reconciling with an Adversary (Matthew 5:21–26|MAT 5:21-26*)
units.rightText: Ye hypocrites, ye know how to interpret the face of the earth and the heaven; but how is it that ye know not how to interpret this time?

units.leftText: And why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?
units.rightText: And why even of yourselves judge ye not what is right?

units.leftText: Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate. Otherwise, he may drag you off to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison.
units.rightText: For as thou art going with thine adversary before the magistrate, on the way give diligence to be quit of him; lest haply he drag thee unto the judge, and the judge shall deliver thee to the officer, and the officer shall cast thee into prison.

units.leftText: I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny. ”
units.rightText: I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou have paid the very last mite.
leftNotes: 12:59 Greek lepton; that is, a Jewish coin of bronze or copper worth about 1/128 of a denarius

units.leftText: At that time some of those present told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
units.rightText: Now there were some present at that very season who told him of the Galilæans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.

units.leftText: To this He replied, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this way?
units.rightText: And he answered and said unto them, Think ye that these Galilæans were sinners above all the Galilæans, because they have suffered these things?

units.leftText: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.
units.rightText: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all in like manner perish.

units.leftText: Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them: Do you think that they were more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?
units.rightText: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and killed them, think ye that they were offenders above all the men that dwell in Jerusalem?

units.leftText: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.” The Parable of the Barren Fig Tree (Isaiah 5:1–7|ISA 5:1-7*)
units.rightText: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

units.leftText: Then Jesus told this parable: “A man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it but did not find any.
units.rightText: And he spake this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came seeking fruit thereon, and found none.

units.leftText: So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, ‘Look, for the past three years I have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’
units.rightText: And he said unto the vinedresser, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why doth it also cumber the ground?
leftNotes: 13:7 SBL, NE, WH Cut it down!

units.leftText: ‘Sir,’ the man replied, ‘leave it alone again this year, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
units.rightText: And he answering saith unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it:

units.leftText: If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down.’” Jesus Heals a Disabled Woman
units.rightText: and if it bear fruit thenceforth, well; but if not, thou shalt cut it down.

units.leftText: One Sabbath Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues,
units.rightText: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath day.

units.leftText: and a woman there had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was hunched over and could not stand up straight.
units.rightText: And behold, a woman that had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years; and she was bowed together, and could in no wise lift herself up.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said, “Woman, you are set free from your disability.”
units.rightText: And when Jesus saw her, he called her, and said to her, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.

units.leftText: Then He placed His hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and began to glorify God.
units.rightText: And he laid his hands upon her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.

units.leftText: But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. “There are six days for work,” he told the crowd. “So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath.”
units.rightText: And the ruler of the synagogue, being moved with indignation because Jesus had healed on the sabbath, answered and said to the multitude, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the day of the sabbath.

units.leftText: “You hypocrites!” the Lord replied. “Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it to water?
units.rightText: But the Lord answered him, and said, Ye hypocrites, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?

units.leftText: Then should not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be released from her bondage on the Sabbath day?”
units.rightText: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had bound, lo, these eighteen years, to have been loosed from this bond on the day of the sabbath?

units.leftText: When Jesus said this, all His adversaries were humiliated. And the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things He was doing. The Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13:31–32|MAT 13:31-32*; Mark 4:30–34|MRK 4:30-34*)
units.rightText: And as he said these things, all his adversaries were put to shame: and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.

units.leftText: Then Jesus asked, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?
units.rightText: He said therefore, Unto what is the kingdom of God like? and whereunto shall I liken it?

units.leftText: It is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.” The Parable of the Leaven (Matthew 13:33|MAT 13:33*)
units.rightText: It is like unto a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his own garden; and it grew, and became a tree; and the birds of the heaven lodged in the branches thereof.

units.leftText: Again He asked, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?
units.rightText: And again he said, Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?

units.leftText: It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.” The Narrow Door (Matthew 7:13–14|MAT 7:13-14*)
units.rightText: It is like unto leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till it was all leavened.

units.leftText: Then Jesus traveled throughout the towns and villages, teaching as He made His way toward Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And he went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and journeying on unto Jerusalem.

units.leftText: “Lord,” someone asked Him, “will only a few people be saved?”
units.rightText: And one said unto him, Lord, are they few that are saved? And he said unto them,

units.leftText: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
units.rightText: Strive to enter in by the narrow door: for many, I say unto you, shall seek to enter in, and shall not be able.

units.leftText: After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, ‘Lord, open the door for us.’ But he will reply, ‘I do not know where you are from.’
units.rightText: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, open to us; and he shall answer and say to you, I know you not whence ye are;

units.leftText: Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’
units.rightText: then shall ye begin to say, We did eat and drink in thy presence, and thou didst teach in our streets;

units.leftText: And he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.’
units.rightText: and he shall say, I tell you, I know not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.

units.leftText: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are thrown out.
units.rightText: There shall be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and yourselves cast forth without.

units.leftText: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
units.rightText: And they shall come from the east and west, and from the north and south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: And indeed, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.” Lament over Jerusalem (Matthew 23:37–39|MAT 23:37-39*)
units.rightText: And behold, there are last who shall be first, and there are first who shall be last.

units.leftText: At that very hour, some Pharisees came to Jesus and told Him, “Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You.”
units.rightText: In that very hour there came certain Pharisees, saying to him, Get thee out, and go hence: for Herod would fain kill thee.

units.leftText: But Jesus replied, “Go tell that fox, ‘Look, I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach My goal.’
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Go and say to that fox, Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures to-day and to-morrow, and the third day I am perfected.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Nevertheless I must go on my way to-day and to-morrow and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
units.rightText: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that killeth the prophets, and stoneth them that are sent unto her! how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her own brood under her wings, and ye would not!

units.leftText: Look, your house is left to you desolate. And I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’ ”
units.rightText: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

units.leftText: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat in the home of a leading Pharisee, and those in attendance were watching Him closely.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a sabbath to eat bread, that they were watching him.

units.leftText: Right there before Him was a man with dropsy.
units.rightText: And behold, there was before him a certain man that had the dropsy.

units.leftText: So Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”
units.rightText: And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath, or not?

units.leftText: But they remained silent.
units.rightText: But they held their peace. And he took him, and healed him, and let him go.

units.leftText: And He asked them, “Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day will not immediately pull him out?”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a well, and will not straightway draw him up on a sabbath day?
leftNotes: 14:5 TR donkey

units.leftText: And they were unable to answer these questions. The Parable of the Guests
units.rightText: And they could not answer again unto these things.

units.leftText: When Jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, He told them a parable:
units.rightText: And he spake a parable unto those that were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief seats; saying unto them,

units.leftText: “When you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited.
units.rightText: When thou art bidden of any man to a marriage feast, sit not down in the chief seat; lest haply a more honorable man than thou be bidden of him,

units.leftText: Then the host who invited both of you will come and tell you, ‘Give this man your seat.’ And in humiliation, you will have to take the last place.
units.rightText: and he that bade thee and him shall come and say to thee, Give this man place; and then thou shalt begin with shame to take the lowest place.

units.leftText: But when you are invited, go and sit in the last place, so that your host will come and tell you, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ Then you will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you.
