units.rightText: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest place; that when he that hath bidden thee cometh, he may say to thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have glory in the presence of all that sit at meat with thee.
leftNotes: 14:10 See Proverbs 25:7|PRO 25:7*.

units.leftText: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
units.rightText: For every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to the man who had invited Him, “When you host a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or brothers or relatives or rich neighbors. Otherwise, they may invite you in return, and you will be repaid.
units.rightText: And he said to him also that had bidden him, When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, nor thy kinsmen, nor rich neighbors; lest haply they also bid thee again, and a recompense be made thee.

units.leftText: But when you host a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind,
units.rightText: But when thou makest a feast, bid the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:

units.leftText: and you will be blessed. Since they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.” The Parable of the Banquet (Matthew 22:1–14|MAT 22:1-14*)
units.rightText: and thou shalt be blessed; because they have not wherewith to recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed in the resurrection of the just.

units.leftText: When one of those reclining with Him heard this, he said to Jesus, “Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.”
units.rightText: And when one of them that sat at meat with him heard these things, he said unto him, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.
leftNotes: 14:15 Literally who will eat bread

units.leftText: But Jesus replied, “A certain man prepared a great banquet and invited many guests.
units.rightText: But he said unto him, A certain man made a great supper; and he bade many:

units.leftText: When it was time for the banquet, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’
units.rightText: and he sent forth his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready.

units.leftText: But one after another they all began to make excuses. The first one said, ‘I have bought a field, and I need to go see it. Please excuse me.’
units.rightText: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a field, and I must needs go out and see it; I pray thee have me excused.

units.leftText: Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.’
units.rightText: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them; I pray thee have me excused.

units.leftText: Still another said, ‘I have married a wife, so I cannot come.’
units.rightText: And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.

units.leftText: The servant returned and reported all this to his master. Then the owner of the house became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city, and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.’
units.rightText: And the servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor and maimed and blind and lame.

units.leftText: ‘Sir,’ the servant replied, ‘what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.’
units.rightText: And the servant said, Lord, what thou didst command is done, and yet there is room.

units.leftText: So the master told his servant, ‘Go out to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full.
units.rightText: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and constrain them to come in, that my house may be filled.

units.leftText: For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my banquet.’” The Cost of Discipleship (Matthew 8:18–22|MAT 8:18-22*; Luke 9:57–62|LUK 9:57-62*; John 6:59–66|JHN 6:59-66*)
units.rightText: For I say unto you, that none of those men that were bidden shall taste of my supper.

units.leftText: Now large crowds were traveling with Jesus, and He turned and said to them,
units.rightText: Now there went with him great multitudes: and he turned, and said unto them,

units.leftText: “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters — yes, even his own life — he cannot be My disciple.
units.rightText: If any man cometh unto me, and hateth not his own father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.

units.leftText: And whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple.
units.rightText: Whosoever doth not bear his own cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.

units.leftText: Which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?
units.rightText: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doth not first sit down and count the cost, whether he have wherewith to complete it?

units.leftText: Otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish the work, everyone who sees it will ridicule him,
units.rightText: Lest haply, when he hath laid a foundation, and is not able to finish, all that behold begin to mock him,

units.leftText: saying, ‘This man could not finish what he started to build.’
units.rightText: saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.

units.leftText: Or what king on his way to war with another king will not first sit down and consider whether he can engage with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
units.rightText: Or what king, as he goeth to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and take counsel whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?

units.leftText: And if he is unable, he will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace.
units.rightText: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and asketh conditions of peace.

units.leftText: In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple. Good Salt (Matthew 5:13–16|MAT 5:13-16*; Mark 9:49–50|MRK 9:49-50*)
units.rightText: So therefore whosoever he be of you that renounceth not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.

units.leftText: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its savor, with what will it be seasoned?
units.rightText: Salt therefore is good: but if even the salt have lost its savor, wherewith shall it be seasoned?

units.leftText: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, and it is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
units.rightText: It is fit neither for the land nor for the dunghill: men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

units.leftText: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were gathering around to listen to Jesus.
units.rightText: Now all the publicans and sinners were drawing near unto him to hear him.

units.leftText: So the Pharisees and scribes began to grumble: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
units.rightText: And both the Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.

units.leftText: Then Jesus told them this parable:
units.rightText: And he spake unto them this parable, saying,

units.leftText: “What man among you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the pasture and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?
units.rightText: What man of you, having a hundred sheep, and having lost one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?

units.leftText: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders,
units.rightText: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

units.leftText: comes home, and calls together his friends and neighbors to tell them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!’
units.rightText: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and his neighbors, saying unto them, Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost.

units.leftText: I tell you that in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need to repent. The Parable of the Lost Coin
units.rightText: I say unto you, that even so there shall be joy in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine righteous persons, who need no repentance.

units.leftText: Or what woman who has ten silver coins and loses one of them does not light a lamp, sweep her house, and search carefully until she finds it?
units.rightText: Or what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a lamp, and sweep the house, and seek diligently until she find it?
leftNotes: 15:8 Greek ten drachmas, each worth about a day’s wages

units.leftText: And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors to say, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost coin.’
units.rightText: And when she hath found it, she calleth together her friends and neighbors, saying, Rejoice with me, for I have found the piece which I had lost.

units.leftText: In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents.” The Parable of the Prodigal Son (Deuteronomy 21:18–21|DEU 21:18-21*)
units.rightText: Even so, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said, “There was a man who had two sons.
units.rightText: And he said, A certain man had two sons:

units.leftText: The younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.
units.rightText: and the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of thy substance that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living.

units.leftText: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.
units.rightText: And not many days after, the younger son gathered all together and took his journey into a far country; and there he wasted his substance with riotous living.

units.leftText: After he had spent all he had, a severe famine swept through that country, and he began to be in need.
units.rightText: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that country; and he began to be in want.

units.leftText: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.
units.rightText: And he went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.

units.leftText: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.
units.rightText: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.

units.leftText: Finally he came to his senses and said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food, but here I am, starving to death!
units.rightText: But when he came to himself he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish here with hunger!

units.leftText: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
units.rightText: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight:

units.leftText: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.”’
units.rightText: I am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

units.leftText: So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.
units.rightText: And he arose, and came to his father. But while he was yet afar off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

units.leftText: The son declared, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son. ’
units.rightText: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight: I am no more worthy to be called thy son.
leftNotes: 15:21 WH includes Make me like one of your hired servants; see verse 19.

units.leftText: But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
units.rightText: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth quickly the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:

units.leftText: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.
units.rightText: and bring the fatted calf, and kill it, and let us eat, and make merry:

units.leftText: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’ So they began to celebrate.
units.rightText: for this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.

units.leftText: Meanwhile the older son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.
units.rightText: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing.

units.leftText: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.
units.rightText: And he called to him one of the servants, and inquired what these things might be.

units.leftText: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.

units.leftText: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.
units.rightText: But he was angry, and would not go in: and his father came out, and entreated him.

units.leftText: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
units.rightText: But he answered and said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, and I never transgressed a commandment of thine; and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:

units.leftText: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’
units.rightText: but when this thy son came, who hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou killedst for him the fatted calf.

units.leftText: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that is mine is thine.

units.leftText: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”
units.rightText: But it was meet to make merry and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.

units.leftText: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.
units.rightText: And he said also unto the disciples, There was a certain rich man, who had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he was wasting his goods.

units.leftText: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’
units.rightText: And he called him, and said unto him, What is this that I hear of thee? render the account of thy stewardship; for thou canst be no longer steward.

units.leftText: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.
units.rightText: And the steward said within himself, What shall I do, seeing that my lord taketh away the stewardship from me? I have not strength to dig; to beg I am ashamed.

units.leftText: I know what I will do so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’
units.rightText: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.

units.leftText: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.
units.rightText: And calling to him each one of his lord’s debtors, he said to the first, How much owest thou unto my lord?

units.leftText: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered. ‘Take your bill,’ said the manager, ‘sit down quickly, and write fifty.’
units.rightText: And he said, A hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bond, and sit down quickly and write fifty.
leftNotes: 16:6 Greek ‘A hundred baths of oil’; that is, approximately 870 gallons or 3,300 liters

units.leftText: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ ‘A hundred measures of wheat,’ he replied. ‘Take your bill and write eighty,’ he told him.
units.rightText: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, A hundred measures of wheat. He saith unto him, Take thy bond, and write fourscore.
leftNotes: 16:7 Greek ‘A hundred cors of wheat’; that is, approximately 1,000 bushels or 35,000 liters (probably about 30 tons or 27 metric tons of wheat)

units.leftText: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.
units.rightText: And his lord commended the unrighteous steward because he had done wisely: for the sons of this world are for their own generation wiser than the sons of the light.

units.leftText: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.
units.rightText: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends by means of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when it shall fail, they may receive you into the eternal tabernacles.

units.leftText: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
units.rightText: He that is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much: and he that is unrighteous in a very little is unrighteous also in much.

units.leftText: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?
units.rightText: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?

units.leftText: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?
units.rightText: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is your own?

units.leftText: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.” The Law and the Prophets
units.rightText: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

units.leftText: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all of this and were scoffing at Jesus.
units.rightText: And the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all these things; and they scoffed at him.

units.leftText: So He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Ye are they that justify yourselves in the sight of men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.

units.leftText: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the gospel of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
units.rightText: The law and the prophets were until John: from that time the gospel of the kingdom of God is preached, and every man entereth violently into it.
leftNotes: 16:16 Or everyone is urged to enter into it

units.leftText: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.
units.rightText: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away, than for one tittle of the law to fall.

units.leftText: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery. The Rich Man and Lazarus (John 5:39–47|JHN 5:39-47*)
units.rightText: Every one that putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery: and he that marrieth one that is put away from a husband committeth adultery.

units.leftText: Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen, who lived each day in joyous splendor.
units.rightText: Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, faring sumptuously every day:

units.leftText: And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores
units.rightText: and a certain beggar named Lazarus was laid at his gate, full of sores,

units.leftText: and longing to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.
units.rightText: and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table; yea, even the dogs came and licked his sores.

units.leftText: One day the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side. And the rich man also died and was buried.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and that he was carried away by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: and the rich man also died, and was buried.
leftNotes: 16:22 Greek into Abraham’s bosom; similarly in verse 23

units.leftText: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.
units.rightText: And in Hades he lifted up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.

units.leftText: So he cried out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. For I am in agony in this fire.’
units.rightText: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am in anguish in this flame.

units.leftText: But Abraham answered, ‘Child, remember that during your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.
units.rightText: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and Lazarus in like manner evil things: but now here he is comforted, and thou art in anguish.

units.leftText: And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you, nor can anyone cross from there to us.’
units.rightText: And besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that they that would pass from hence to you may not be able, and that none may cross over from thence to us.

units.leftText: ‘Then I beg you, father,’ he said, ‘send Lazarus to my father’s house,
units.rightText: And he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house;

units.leftText: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also end up in this place of torment.’
units.rightText: for I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.

units.leftText: But Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let your brothers listen to them.’
units.rightText: But Abraham saith, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.

units.leftText: ‘No, father Abraham,’ he said, ‘but if someone is sent to them from the dead, they will repent.’
units.rightText: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one go to them from the dead, they will repent.

units.leftText: Then Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, if one rise from the dead.

units.leftText: Jesus said to His disciples, “It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!
units.rightText: And he said unto his disciples, It is impossible but that occasions of stumbling should come; but woe unto him, through whom they come!

units.leftText: It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
units.rightText: It were well for him if a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.

units.leftText: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
units.rightText: Take heed to yourselves: if thy brother sin, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.

units.leftText: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.” The Power of Faith (Matthew 17:19–20|MAT 17:19-20*)
units.rightText: And if he sin against thee seven times in the day, and seven times turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.

units.leftText: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”
units.rightText: And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith.

units.leftText: And the Lord answered, “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.
units.rightText: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye would say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou rooted up, and be thou planted in the sea; and it would obey you.

units.leftText: Which of you whose servant comes in from plowing or shepherding in the field will say to him, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?
units.rightText: But who is there of you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say unto him, when he is come in from the field, Come straightway and sit down to meat;

units.leftText: Instead, won’t he tell him, ‘Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink, and afterward you may eat and drink’?
units.rightText: and will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?

units.leftText: Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told?
units.rightText: Doth he thank the servant because he did the things that were commanded?

units.leftText: So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’” The Ten Lepers (2 Kings 5:1–14|2KI 5:1-14*)
units.rightText: Even so ye also, when ye shall have done all the things that are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants; we have done that which it was our duty to do.

units.leftText: While Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem, He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as they were on the way to Jerusalem, that he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.

units.leftText: As He entered one of the villages, He was met by ten lepers. They stood at a distance
units.rightText: And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, who stood afar off:
leftNotes: 17:12 A leper was one afflicted with a skin disease. See Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: and raised their voices, shouting, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
units.rightText: and they lifted up their voices, saying, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw them, He said, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.
units.rightText: And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go and show yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, as they went, they were cleansed.
leftNotes: 17:14 See Leviticus 14:1–32|LEV 14:1-32*.

units.leftText: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God in a loud voice.
units.rightText: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, with a loud voice glorifying God;

units.leftText: He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him — and he was a Samaritan.
units.rightText: and he fell upon his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.

units.leftText: “Were not all ten cleansed?” Jesus asked. “Where then are the other nine?
units.rightText: And Jesus answering said, Were not the ten cleansed? but where are the nine?

units.leftText: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”
units.rightText: Were there none found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger?

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well! ” The Coming of the Kingdom (Genesis 19:24–29|GEN 19:24-29*)
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Arise, and go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.
leftNotes: 17:19 Or has saved you

units.leftText: When asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, Jesus replied, “The kingdom of God will not come with observable signs.
units.rightText: And being asked by the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God cometh, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation:

units.leftText: Nor will people say, ‘Look, here it is,’ or ‘There it is.’ For you see, the kingdom of God is in your midst. ”
units.rightText: neither shall they say, Lo, here! or, There! for lo, the kingdom of God is within you.
leftNotes: 17:21 Or within you or within your grasp

units.leftText: Then He said to the disciples, “The time is coming when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.
units.rightText: And he said unto the disciples, The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it.

units.leftText: People will tell you, ‘Look, there He is!’ or ‘Look, here He is!’ Do not go out or chase after them.
units.rightText: And they shall say to you, Lo, there! Lo, here! go not away, nor follow after them:

units.leftText: For just as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will be the Son of Man in His day.
units.rightText: for as the lightning, when it lighteneth out of the one part under the heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall the Son of man be in his day.

units.leftText: But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
units.rightText: But first must he suffer many things and be rejected of this generation.

units.leftText: Just as it was in the days of Noah, so also will it be in the days of the Son of Man:
units.rightText: And as it came to pass in the days of Noah, even so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.

units.leftText: People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.
units.rightText: They ate, they drank, they married, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.

units.leftText: It was the same in the days of Lot: People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.
units.rightText: Likewise even as it came to pass in the days of Lot; they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;

units.leftText: But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.
units.rightText: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all:

units.leftText: It will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
units.rightText: after the same manner shall it be in the day that the Son of man is revealed.

units.leftText: On that day, let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve his possessions. Likewise, let no one in the field return for anything he has left behind.
units.rightText: In that day, he that shall be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away: and let him that is in the field likewise not return back.

units.leftText: Remember Lot’s wife!
units.rightText: Remember Lot’s wife.

units.leftText: Whoever tries to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will preserve it.
units.rightText: Whosoever shall seek to gain his life shall lose it: but whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it.

units.leftText: I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed: one will be taken and the other left.
units.rightText: I say unto you, In that night there shall be two men on one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.

units.leftText: Two women will be grinding grain together: one will be taken and the other left.”
units.rightText: There shall be two women grinding together; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.
leftNotes: 17:35 TR includes 36*Two men will be in the field. One will be taken and the other left; see Matthew 24:40|MAT 24:40*.

rightNotes: 17:36 Some ancient authorities add v. 36. There shall be two men in the field; the one shall be taken and the other shall be left. Mat 24:40

units.leftText: “Where, Lord?” they asked. Jesus answered, “Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.”
units.rightText: And they answering say unto him, Where, Lord? And he said unto them, Where the body is, thither will the eagles also be gathered together.

units.leftText: Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart:
units.rightText: And he spake a parable unto them to the end that they ought always to pray, and not to faint;

units.leftText: “In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected men.
units.rightText: saying, There was in a city a judge, who feared not God, and regarded not man:

units.leftText: And there was a widow in that town who kept appealing to him, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’
units.rightText: and there was a widow in that city; and she came oft unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.

units.leftText: For a while he refused, but later he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect men,
units.rightText: And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man;

units.leftText: yet because this widow keeps pestering me, I will give her justice. Otherwise, she will wear me out with her perpetual requests.’”
units.rightText: yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest she wear me out by her continual coming.

units.leftText: And the Lord said, “Listen to the words of the unjust judge.
units.rightText: And the Lord said, Hear what the unrighteous judge saith.

units.leftText: Will not God bring about justice for His elect who cry out to Him day and night? Will He delay in helping them?
units.rightText: And shall not God avenge his elect, that cry to him day and night, and yet he is longsuffering over them?

units.leftText: I tell you, He will promptly carry out justice on their behalf. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on earth?” The Pharisee and the Tax Collector
units.rightText: I say unto you, that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?

units.leftText: To some who trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt, He also told this parable:
units.rightText: And he spake also this parable unto certain who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and set all others at nought:

units.leftText: “Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
units.rightText: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.

units.leftText: The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, ‘God, I thank You that I am not like other men — swindlers, evildoers, adulterers — or even like this tax collector.
units.rightText: The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as the rest of men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican.
leftNotes: 18:11 Or stood and prayed to himself

units.leftText: I fast twice a week and pay tithes of all that I acquire.’
units.rightText: I fast twice in the week; I give tithes of all that I get.

units.leftText: But the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his breast and said, ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner!’
units.rightText: But the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote his breast, saying, God, be thou merciful to me a sinner.

units.leftText: I tell you, this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.” Jesus Blesses the Children (Matthew 19:13–15|MAT 19:13-15*; Mark 10:13–16|MRK 10:13-16*)
units.rightText: I say unto you, This man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be humbled; but he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

units.leftText: Now people were even bringing their babies to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them. And when the disciples saw this, they rebuked those who brought them.
units.rightText: And they were bringing unto him also their babes, that he should touch them: but when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.

units.leftText: But Jesus called the children to Him and said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
units.rightText: But Jesus called them unto him, saying, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for to such belongeth the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.” The Rich Young Ruler (Matthew 19:16–30|MAT 19:16-30*; Mark 10:17–31|MRK 10:17-31*)
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall in no wise enter therein.

units.leftText: Then a certain ruler asked Him, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
units.rightText: And a certain ruler asked him, saying, Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?

units.leftText: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? none is good, save one, even God.

units.leftText: You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.’ ”
units.rightText: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honor thy father and mother.

units.leftText: “All these I have kept from my youth,” he said.
units.rightText: And he said, All these things have I observed from my youth up.

units.leftText: On hearing this, Jesus told him, “You still lack one thing: Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”
units.rightText: And when Jesus heard it, he said unto him, One thing thou lackest yet: sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.

units.leftText: But when the ruler heard this, he became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy.
units.rightText: But when he heard these things, he became exceeding sorrowful; for he was very rich.

units.leftText: Seeing the man’s sadness, Jesus said, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!
units.rightText: And Jesus seeing him said, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!
leftNotes: 18:24 Literally Seeing that he had become sorrowful; SBL, NE, and WH Seeing him

units.leftText: Indeed, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”
units.rightText: For it is easier for a camel to enter in through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: Those who heard this asked, “Who then can be saved?”
units.rightText: And they that heard it said, Then who can be saved?

units.leftText: But Jesus said, “What is impossible with man is possible with God.”
units.rightText: But he said, The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.

units.leftText: “Look,” said Peter, “we have left all we had to follow You.”
units.rightText: And Peter said, Lo, we have left our own, and followed thee.
leftNotes: 18:28 Literally left our own; BYZ and TR left all

units.leftText: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or wife, or brethren, or parents, or children, for the kingdom of God’s sake,

units.leftText: will fail to receive many times more in this age — and in the age to come, eternal life.” The Third Prediction of the Passion (Matthew 20:17–19|MAT 20:17-19*; Mark 10:32–34|MRK 10:32-34*)
units.rightText: who shall not receive manifold more in this time, and in the world to come eternal life.

units.leftText: Then Jesus took the Twelve aside and said to them, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
units.rightText: And he took unto him the twelve, and said unto them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all the things that are written through the prophets shall be accomplished unto the Son of man.

units.leftText: He will be delivered over to the Gentiles and will be mocked and insulted and spit upon.
units.rightText: For he shall be delivered up unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and shamefully treated, and spit upon:

units.leftText: They will flog Him and kill Him, and on the third day He will rise again.”
units.rightText: and they shall scourge and kill him: and the third day he shall rise again.

units.leftText: But the disciples did not understand any of these things. The meaning was hidden from them, and they did not comprehend what He was saying. Jesus Heals a Blind Beggar (Matthew 20:29–34|MAT 20:29-34*; Mark 10:46–52|MRK 10:46-52*)
units.rightText: And they understood none of these things; and this saying was hid from them, and they perceived not the things that were said.

units.leftText: As Jesus drew near to Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as he drew nigh unto Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way side begging:

units.leftText: When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.
units.rightText: and hearing a multitude going by, he inquired what this meant.

units.leftText: “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by,” they told him.
units.rightText: And they told him, that Jesus of Nazareth passeth by.

units.leftText: So he called out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
units.rightText: And he cried, saying, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.

units.leftText: Those who led the way admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
units.rightText: And they that went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried out the more a great deal, Thou son of David, have mercy on me.

units.leftText: Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him. When he had come near, Jesus asked him,
units.rightText: And Jesus stood, and commanded him to be brought unto him: and when he was come near, he asked him,

units.leftText: “What do you want Me to do for you?” “Lord,” he said, “let me see again.”
units.rightText: What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? And he said, Lord, that I may receive my sight.

units.leftText: “Receive your sight!” Jesus replied. “Your faith has healed you.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto him, Receive thy sight: thy faith hath made thee whole.

units.leftText: Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus, glorifying God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.
units.rightText: And immediately he received his sight, and followed him, glorifying God: and all the people, when they saw it, gave praise unto God.

units.leftText: Then Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through.
units.rightText: And he entered and was passing through Jericho.

units.leftText: And there was a man named Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, who was very wealthy.
units.rightText: And behold, a man called by name Zacchæus; and he was a chief publican, and he was rich.

units.leftText: He was trying to see who Jesus was, but could not see over the crowd because he was small in stature.
units.rightText: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the crowd, because he was little of stature.

units.leftText: So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Him, since Jesus was about to pass that way.
units.rightText: And he ran on before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.

units.leftText: When Jesus came to that place, He looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry down, for I must stay at your house today.”
units.rightText: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and said unto him, Zacchæus, make haste, and come down; for to-day I must abide at thy house.

units.leftText: So Zacchaeus hurried down and welcomed Him joyfully.
units.rightText: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.

units.leftText: And all who saw this began to grumble, saying, “He has gone to be the guest of a sinful man!”
units.rightText: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, He is gone in to lodge with a man that is a sinner.

units.leftText: But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, “Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone, I will repay it fourfold.”
units.rightText: And Zacchæus stood, and said unto the Lord, Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have wrongfully exacted aught of any man, I restore fourfold.

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because this man too is a son of Abraham.
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto him, To-day is salvation come to this house, forasmuch as he also is a son of Abraham.

units.leftText: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.” The Parable of the Ten Minas (Matthew 25:14–30|MAT 25:14-30*)
units.rightText: For the Son of man came to seek and to save that which was lost.

units.leftText: While the people were listening to this, Jesus proceeded to tell them a parable, because He was near Jerusalem and they thought the kingdom of God would appear imminently.
units.rightText: And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they supposed that the kingdom of God was immediately to appear.

units.leftText: So He said, “A man of noble birth went to a distant country to lay claim to his kingship and then return.
units.rightText: He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country, to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.

units.leftText: Beforehand, he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas. ‘Conduct business with this until I return,’ he said.
units.rightText: And he called ten servants of his, and gave them ten pounds, and said unto them, Trade ye herewith till I come.
leftNotes: 19:13 That is, he gave each servant one mina. A mina was most likely a silver coin worth a hundred drachmas, that is, about a hundred days’ wages.

units.leftText: But his subjects hated him and sent a delegation after him to say, ‘We do not want this man to rule over us.’
units.rightText: But his citizens hated him, and sent an ambassage after him, saying, We will not that this man reign over us.

units.leftText: When he returned from procuring his kingship, he summoned the servants to whom he had given the money, to find out what each one had earned.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he was come back again, having received the kingdom, that he commanded these servants, unto whom he had given the money, to be called to him, that he might know what they had gained by trading.

units.leftText: The first servant came forward and said, ‘Master, your mina has produced ten more minas.’
units.rightText: And the first came before him, saying, Lord, thy pound hath made ten pounds more.

units.leftText: His master replied, ‘Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter, you shall have authority over ten cities.’
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Well done, thou good servant: because thou wast found faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.

units.leftText: The second servant came and said, ‘Master, your mina has made five minas.’
units.rightText: And the second came, saying, Thy pound, Lord, hath made five pounds.

units.leftText: And to this one he said, ‘You shall have authority over five cities.’
units.rightText: And he said unto him also, Be thou also over five cities.

units.leftText: Then another servant came and said, ‘Master, here is your mina, which I have laid away in a piece of cloth.
units.rightText: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I kept laid up in a napkin:
leftNotes: 19:20 Greek soudariō

units.leftText: For I was afraid of you, because you are a harsh man. You withdraw what you did not deposit and reap what you did not sow.’
units.rightText: for I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that which thou layedst not down, and reapest that which thou didst not sow.

units.leftText: His master replied, ‘You wicked servant, I will judge you by your own words. So you knew that I am a harsh man, withdrawing what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow?
units.rightText: He saith unto him, Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Thou knewest that I am an austere man, taking up that which I laid not down, and reaping that which I did not sow;

units.leftText: Why then did you not deposit my money in the bank, and upon my return I could have collected it with interest?’
units.rightText: then wherefore gavest thou not my money into the bank, and I at my coming should have required it with interest?

units.leftText: Then he told those standing by, ‘Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has ten minas.’
units.rightText: And he said unto them that stood by, Take away from him the pound, and give it unto him that hath the ten pounds.

units.leftText: ‘Master,’ they said, ‘he already has ten!’
units.rightText: And they said unto him, Lord, he hath ten pounds.

units.leftText: He replied, ‘ I tell you that everyone who has will be given more; but the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
units.rightText: I say unto you, that unto every one that hath shall be given; but from him that hath not, even that which he hath shall be taken away from him.

units.leftText: And these enemies of mine who were unwilling for me to rule over them, bring them here and slay them in front of me.’” The Triumphal Entry (Zechariah 9:9–13|ZEC 9:9-13*; Matthew 21:1–11|MAT 21:1-11*; Mark 11:1–11|MRK 11:1-11*; John 12:12–19|JHN 12:12-19*)
units.rightText: But these mine enemies, that would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.

units.leftText: After Jesus had said this, He went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And when he had thus spoken, he went on before, going up to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: As He approached Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, He sent out two of His disciples,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he drew nigh unto Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount that is called Olivet, he sent two of the disciples,

units.leftText: saying, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.
units.rightText: saying, Go your way into the village over against you; in which as ye enter ye shall find a colt tied, whereon no man ever yet sat: loose him, and bring him.

units.leftText: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying it?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it.’”
units.rightText: And if any one ask you, Why do ye loose him? thus shall ye say, The Lord hath need of him.

units.leftText: So those who were sent went out and found it just as Jesus had told them.
units.rightText: And they that were sent went away, and found even as he had said unto them.

units.leftText: As they were untying the colt, its owners asked, “Why are you untying the colt?”
units.rightText: And as they were loosing the colt, the owners thereof said unto them, Why loose ye the colt?

units.leftText: “The Lord needs it,” they answered.
units.rightText: And they said, The Lord hath need of him.

units.leftText: Then they led the colt to Jesus, threw their cloaks over it, and put Jesus on it.
units.rightText: And they brought him to Jesus: and they threw their garments upon the colt, and set Jesus thereon.

units.leftText: As He rode along, the people spread their cloaks on the road.
units.rightText: And as he went, they spread their garments in the way.

units.leftText: And as He approached the descent from the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of disciples began to praise God joyfully in a loud voice for all the miracles they had seen:
units.rightText: And as he was now drawing nigh, even at the descent of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which they had seen;

units.leftText: “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
units.rightText: saying, Blessed is the King that cometh in the name of the Lord: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.

units.leftText: But some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, rebuke Your disciples!”
units.rightText: And some of the Pharisees from the multitude said unto him, Teacher, rebuke thy disciples.

units.leftText: “I tell you,” He answered, “if they remain silent, the very stones will cry out.” Jesus Weeps over Jerusalem (Isaiah 29:1–16|ISA 29:1-16*)
units.rightText: And he answered and said, I tell you that, if these shall hold their peace, the stones will cry out.

units.leftText: As Jesus approached Jerusalem and saw the city, He wept over it
units.rightText: And when he drew nigh, he saw the city and wept over it,

units.leftText: and said, “If only you had known on this day what would bring you peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.
units.rightText: saying, If thou hadst known in this day, even thou, the things which belong unto peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.

units.leftText: For the days will come upon you when your enemies will barricade you and surround you and hem you in on every side.
units.rightText: For the days shall come upon thee, when thine enemies shall cast up a bank about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,

units.leftText: They will level you to the ground — you and the children within your walls. They will not leave one stone on another, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation from God. ” Jesus Cleanses the Temple (Matthew 21:12–17|MAT 21:12-17*; Mark 11:15–19|MRK 11:15-19*; John 2:12–25|JHN 2:12-25*)
units.rightText: and shall dash thee to the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
leftNotes: 19:44 Literally your visitation

units.leftText: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were selling there.
units.rightText: And he entered into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold,
leftNotes: 19:45 Literally the temple

units.leftText: He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be a house of prayer.’ But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’ ”
units.rightText: saying unto them, It is written, And my house shall be a house of prayer: but ye have made it a den of robbers.
leftNotes: 19:46 Jeremiah 7:11|JER 7:11*

units.leftText: Jesus was teaching at the temple every day, but the chief priests, scribes, and leaders of the people were intent on killing Him.
units.rightText: And he was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the principal men of the people sought to destroy him:

units.leftText: Yet they could not find a way to do so, because all the people hung on His words.
units.rightText: and they could not find what they might do; for the people all hung upon him, listening.

units.leftText: One day as Jesus was teaching the people in the temple courts and proclaiming the gospel, the chief priests and scribes, together with the elders, came up to Him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, on one of the days, as he was teaching the people in the temple, and preaching the gospel, there came upon him the chief priests and the scribes with the elders;
leftNotes: 20:1 Literally the temple

units.leftText: “Tell us,” they said, “by what authority are You doing these things, and who gave You this authority?”
units.rightText: and they spake, saying unto him, Tell us: By what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?

units.leftText: “I will also ask you a question,” Jesus replied. “Tell Me:
units.rightText: And he answered and said unto them, I also will ask you a question; and tell me:

units.leftText: John’s baptism — was it from heaven, or from men?”
units.rightText: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men?

units.leftText: They deliberated among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why did you not believe him?’
units.rightText: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why did ye not believe him?

units.leftText: But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet.”
units.rightText: But if we shall say, From men; all the people will stone us: for they are persuaded that John was a prophet.

units.leftText: So they answered that they did not know where it was from.
units.rightText: And they answered, that they knew not whence it was.

units.leftText: And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.” The Parable of the Wicked Tenants (Matthew 21:33–46|MAT 21:33-46*; Mark 12:1–12|MRK 12:1-12*)
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.

units.leftText: Then He proceeded to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, rented it out to some tenants, and went away for a long time.
units.rightText: And he began to speak unto the people this parable: A man planted a vineyard, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into another country for a long time.

units.leftText: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants beat the servant and sent him away empty-handed.
units.rightText: And at the season he sent unto the husbandmen a servant, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.

units.leftText: So he sent another servant, but they beat him and treated him shamefully, sending him away empty-handed.
units.rightText: And he sent yet another servant: and him also they beat, and handled him shamefully, and sent him away empty.

units.leftText: Then he sent a third, but they wounded him and threw him out.
units.rightText: And he sent yet a third: and him also they wounded, and cast him forth.

units.leftText: ‘What shall I do?’ asked the owner of the vineyard. ‘I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect him.’
units.rightText: And the lord of the vineyard said, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; it may be they will reverence him.

units.leftText: But when the tenants saw the son, they discussed it among themselves and said, ‘This is the heir. Let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
units.rightText: But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned one with another, saying, This is the heir; let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.

units.leftText: So they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
units.rightText: And they cast him forth out of the vineyard, and killed him. What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do unto them?

units.leftText: He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others.” And when the people heard this, they said, “May such a thing never happen!”
units.rightText: He will come and destroy these husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others. And when they heard it, they said, God forbid.

units.leftText: But Jesus looked directly at them and said, “Then what is the meaning of that which is written: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone’ ?
units.rightText: But he looked upon them, and said, What then is this that is written, The stone which the builders rejected, The same was made the head of the corner?

units.leftText: Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed.” Paying Taxes to Caesar (Matthew 22:15–22|MAT 22:15-22*; Mark 12:13–17|MRK 12:13-17*)
units.rightText: Every one that falleth on that stone shall be broken to pieces; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will scatter him as dust.

units.leftText: When the scribes and chief priests realized that Jesus had spoken this parable against them, they sought to arrest Him that very hour. But they were afraid of the people.
units.rightText: And the scribes and the chief priests sought to lay hands on him in that very hour; and they feared the people: for they perceived that he spake this parable against them.

units.leftText: So they watched Him closely and sent spies who pretended to be sincere. They were hoping to catch Him in His words in order to hand Him over to the rule and authority of the governor.
units.rightText: And they watched him, and sent forth spies, who feigned themselves to be righteous, that they might take hold of his speech, so as to deliver him up to the rule and to the authority of the governor.

units.leftText: “Teacher,” they inquired, “we know that You speak and teach correctly. You show no partiality but teach the way of God in accordance with the truth.
units.rightText: And they asked him, saying, Teacher, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly, and acceptest not the person of any, but of a truth teachest the way of God:

units.leftText: Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
units.rightText: Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Cæsar, or not?

units.leftText: But Jesus saw through their duplicity and said to them,
units.rightText: But he perceived their craftiness, and said unto them,

units.leftText: “Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription are on it?” “Caesar’s,” they answered.
units.rightText: Show me a denarius. Whose image and superscription hath it? And they said, Cæsar’s.
leftNotes: 20:24 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: So Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Then render unto Cæsar the things that are Cæsar’s, and unto God the things that are God’s.

units.leftText: And they were unable to trap Him in His words before the people. And amazed at His answer, they fell silent. The Sadducees and the Resurrection (Matthew 22:23–33|MAT 22:23-33*; Mark 12:18–27|MRK 12:18-27*)
units.rightText: And they were not able to take hold of the saying before the people: and they marvelled at his answer, and held their peace.

units.leftText: Then some of the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to question Him.
units.rightText: And there came to him certain of the Sadducees, they that say that there is no resurrection;

units.leftText: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.
units.rightText: and they asked him, saying, Teacher, Moses wrote unto us, that if a man’s brother die, having a wife, and he be childless, his brother should take the wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
leftNotes: 20:28 Deuteronomy 25:5|DEU 25:5*

units.leftText: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married a wife but died childless.
units.rightText: There were therefore seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and died childless;

units.leftText: Then the second
units.rightText: and the second:
leftNotes: 20:30 BYZ and TR include married the widow, and he also died,

units.leftText: and the third married the widow, and in the same way all seven died, leaving no children.
units.rightText: and the third took her; and likewise the seven also left no children, and died.

units.leftText: And last of all, the woman died.
units.rightText: Afterward the woman also died.

units.leftText: So then, in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”
units.rightText: In the resurrection therefore whose wife of them shall she be? for the seven had her to wife.

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, The sons of this world marry, and are given in marriage:

units.leftText: But those who are considered worthy to share in the age to come and in the resurrection from the dead will neither marry nor be given in marriage.
units.rightText: but they that are accounted worthy to attain to that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage:

units.leftText: In fact, they can no longer die, because they are like the angels. And since they are sons of the resurrection, they are sons of God.
units.rightText: for neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.

units.leftText: Even Moses demonstrates that the dead are raised, in the passage about the burning bush. For he calls the Lord ‘the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
units.rightText: But that the dead are raised, even Moses showed, in the place concerning the Bush, when he calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
leftNotes: 20:37 Exodus 3:6|EXO 3:6*

units.leftText: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living, for to Him all are alive.”
units.rightText: Now he is not the God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.

units.leftText: Some of the scribes answered, “Teacher, You have spoken well!”
units.rightText: And certain of the scribes answering said, Teacher, thou hast well said.

units.leftText: And they did not dare to question Him any further. Whose Son Is the Christ? (Matthew 22:41–46|MAT 22:41-46*; Mark 12:35–37|MRK 12:35-37*)
units.rightText: For they durst not any more ask him any question.

units.leftText: Then Jesus declared, “How can it be said that the Christ is the Son of David?
units.rightText: And he said unto them, How say they that the Christ is David’s son?

units.leftText: For David himself says in the book of Psalms: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand
units.rightText: For David himself saith in the book of Psalms, The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,

units.leftText: until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”’
units.rightText: Till I make thine enemies the footstool of thy feet.

units.leftText: Thus David calls Him ‘Lord.’ So how can He be David’s son?” Beware of the Scribes (Mark 12:38–40|MRK 12:38-40*)
units.rightText: David therefore calleth him Lord, and how is he his son?

units.leftText: In the hearing of all the people, Jesus said to His disciples,
units.rightText: And in the hearing of all the people he said unto his disciples,

units.leftText: “Beware of the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, and they love the greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets.
units.rightText: Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk in long robes, and love salutations in the marketplaces, and chief seats in the synagogues, and chief places at feasts;

units.leftText: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.”
units.rightText: who devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayers: these shall receive greater condemnation.
leftNotes: 20:47 Literally They devour widows’ houses

units.leftText: Then Jesus looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury,
units.rightText: And he looked up, and saw the rich men that were casting their gifts into the treasury.

units.leftText: and He saw a poor widow put in two small copper coins.
units.rightText: And he saw a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites.
leftNotes: 21:2 Greek two lepta; a lepton was a Jewish coin of bronze or copper worth about 1/128 of a denarius.

units.leftText: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “this poor widow has put in more than all the others.
units.rightText: And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, This poor widow cast in more than they all:

units.leftText: For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.” Temple Destruction and Other Signs (Matthew 24:1–8|MAT 24:1-8*; Mark 13:1–8|MRK 13:1-8*)
units.rightText: for all these did of their superfluity cast in unto the gifts; but she of her want did cast in all the living that she had.

units.leftText: As some of the disciples were remarking how the temple was adorned with beautiful stones and consecrated gifts, Jesus said,
units.rightText: And as some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and offerings, he said,

units.leftText: “As for what you see here, the time will come when not one stone will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”
units.rightText: As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in which there shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.

units.leftText: “Teacher,” they asked, “when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?”
units.rightText: And they asked him, saying, Teacher, when therefore shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when these things are about to come to pass?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “See to it that you are not deceived. For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am He,’ and, ‘The time is near.’ Do not follow them.
units.rightText: And he said, Take heed that ye be not led astray: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am he; and, The time is at hand: go ye not after them.

units.leftText: When you hear of wars and rebellions, do not be alarmed. These things must happen first, but the end is not imminent.” Witnessing to All Nations (Matthew 24:9–14|MAT 24:9-14*; Mark 13:9–13|MRK 13:9-13*)
units.rightText: And when ye shall hear of wars and tumults, be not terrified: for these things must needs come to pass first; but the end is not immediately.

units.leftText: Then He told them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
units.rightText: Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom;

units.leftText: There will be great earthquakes, famines, and pestilences in various places, along with fearful sights and great signs from heaven.
units.rightText: and there shall be great earthquakes, and in divers places famines and pestilences; and there shall be terrors and great signs from heaven.

units.leftText: But before all this, they will seize you and persecute you. On account of My name they will deliver you to the synagogues and prisons, and they will bring you before kings and governors.
units.rightText: But before all these things, they shall lay their hands on you, and shall persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues and prisons, bringing you before kings and governors for my name’s sake.

units.leftText: This will be your opportunity to serve as witnesses.
units.rightText: It shall turn out unto you for a testimony.

units.leftText: So make up your mind not to worry beforehand how to defend yourselves.
units.rightText: Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate beforehand how to answer:

units.leftText: For I will give you speech and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict.
units.rightText: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to withstand or to gainsay.

units.leftText: You will be betrayed even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and some of you will be put to death.
units.rightText: But ye shall be delivered up even by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolk, and friends; and some of you shall they cause to be put to death.

units.leftText: And you will be hated by everyone because of My name.
units.rightText: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake.

units.leftText: Yet not even a hair of your head will perish.
units.rightText: And not a hair of your head shall perish.

units.leftText: By your patient endurance you will gain your souls. The Destruction of Jerusalem (Matthew 24:15–25|MAT 24:15-25*; Mark 13:14–23|MRK 13:14-23*)
units.rightText: In your patience ye shall win your souls.

units.leftText: But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, you will know that her desolation is near.
units.rightText: But when ye see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that her desolation is at hand.

units.leftText: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, let those in the city get out, and let those in the country stay out of the city.
units.rightText: Then let them that are in Judæa flee unto the mountains; and let them that are in the midst of her depart out; and let not them that are in the country enter therein.

units.leftText: For these are the days of vengeance, to fulfill all that is written.
units.rightText: For these are days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.

units.leftText: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people.
units.rightText: Woe unto them that are with child and to them that give suck in those days! for there shall be great distress upon the land, and wrath unto this people.

units.leftText: They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led captive into all the nations. And Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled. The Return of the Son of Man (Matthew 24:26–31|MAT 24:26-31*; Mark 13:24–27|MRK 13:24-27*)
units.rightText: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led captive into all the nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

units.leftText: There will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth dismay among the nations, bewildered by the roaring of the sea and the surging of the waves.
units.rightText: And there shall be signs in sun and moon and stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, in perplexity for the roaring of the sea and the billows;

units.leftText: Men will faint from fear and anxiety over what is coming upon the earth, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
units.rightText: men fainting for fear, and for expectation of the things which are coming on the world: for the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.

units.leftText: At that time they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
units.rightText: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

units.leftText: When these things begin to happen, stand up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near.” The Lesson of the Fig Tree (Matthew 24:32–35|MAT 24:32-35*; Mark 13:28–31|MRK 13:28-31*)
units.rightText: But when these things begin to come to pass, look up, and lift up your heads; because your redemption draweth nigh.

units.leftText: Then Jesus told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees.
units.rightText: And he spake to them a parable: Behold the fig tree, and all the trees:

units.leftText: When they sprout leaves, you can see for yourselves and know that summer is near.
units.rightText: when they now shoot forth, ye see it and know of your own selves that the summer is now nigh.

units.leftText: So also, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
units.rightText: Even so ye also, when ye see these things coming to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all things be accomplished.

units.leftText: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away. Be Watchful for the Day
units.rightText: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

units.leftText: But watch yourselves, or your hearts will be weighed down by dissipation, drunkenness, and the worries of life — and that day will spring upon you suddenly like a snare.
units.rightText: But take heed to yourselves, lest haply your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that day come on you suddenly as a snare:

units.leftText: For it will come upon all who dwell on the face of all the earth.
units.rightText: for so shall it come upon all them that dwell on the face of all the earth.

units.leftText: So keep watch at all times, and pray that you may have the strength to escape all that is about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.”
