units.rightText: But watch ye at every season, making supplication, that ye may prevail to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.

units.leftText: Every day Jesus taught at the temple, but every evening He went out to spend the night on the Mount of Olives.
units.rightText: And every day he was teaching in the temple; and every night he went out, and lodged in the mount that is called Olivet.

units.leftText: And early in the morning all the people would come to hear Him at the temple.
units.rightText: And all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple, to hear him.

units.leftText: Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread, called the Passover, was approaching,
units.rightText: Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.
leftNotes: 22:1 Literally the feast of the Unleavened; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.

units.leftText: and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a way to put Jesus to death, for they feared the people. Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus (Matthew 26:14–16|MAT 26:14-16*; Mark 14:10–11|MRK 14:10-11*)
units.rightText: And the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might put him to death; for they feared the people.

units.leftText: Then Satan entered Judas Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve.
units.rightText: And Satan entered into Judas who was called Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.

units.leftText: And Judas went to discuss with the chief priests and temple officers how he might betray Jesus to them.
units.rightText: And he went away, and communed with the chief priests and captains, how he might deliver him unto them.

units.leftText: They were delighted and agreed to give him money.
units.rightText: And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.

units.leftText: Judas consented, and began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus to them in the absence of a crowd. Preparing the Passover (Matthew 26:17–19|MAT 26:17-19*; Mark 14:12–16|MRK 14:12-16*)
units.rightText: And he consented, and sought opportunity to deliver him unto them in the absence of the multitude.

units.leftText: Then came the day of Unleavened Bread on which the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed.
units.rightText: And the day of unleavened bread came, on which the passover must be sacrificed.

units.leftText: Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, “Go and make preparations for us to eat the Passover.”
units.rightText: And he sent Peter and John, saying, Go and make ready for us the passover, that we may eat.

units.leftText: “Where do You want us to prepare it?” they asked.
units.rightText: And they said unto him, Where wilt thou that we make ready?

units.leftText: He answered, “When you enter the city, a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him to the house he enters,
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Behold, when ye are entered into the city, there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water; follow him into the house whereinto he goeth.

units.leftText: and say to the owner of that house, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’
units.rightText: And ye shall say unto the master of the house, The Teacher saith unto thee, Where is the guest-chamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?

units.leftText: And he will show you a large upper room, already furnished. Make preparations there.”
units.rightText: And he will show you a large upper room furnished: there make ready.

units.leftText: So they went and found it just as Jesus had told them. And they prepared the Passover. The Last Supper (Matthew 26:20–30|MAT 26:20-30*; Mark 14:17–26|MRK 14:17-26*; 1 Corinthians 11:17–34|1CO 11:17-34*)
units.rightText: And they went, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover.

units.leftText: When the hour had come, Jesus reclined at the table with His apostles.
units.rightText: And when the hour was come, he sat down, and the apostles with him.

units.leftText: And He said to them, “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before My suffering.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer:

units.leftText: For I tell you that I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”
units.rightText: for I say unto you, I shall not eat it, until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: After taking the cup, He gave thanks and said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves.
units.rightText: And he received a cup, and when he had given thanks, he said, Take this, and divide it among yourselves:

units.leftText: For I tell you that I will not drink of the fruit of the vine from now on until the kingdom of God comes.”
units.rightText: for I say unto you, I shall not drink from henceforth of the fruit of the vine, until the kingdom of God shall come.

units.leftText: And He took the bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body, given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
units.rightText: And he took bread, and when he had given thanks, he brake it, and gave to them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

units.leftText: In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you.
units.rightText: And the cup in like manner after supper, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood, even that which is poured out for you.
leftNotes: 22:20 Some manuscripts end verse 19 after This is My body and do not include verse 20.

units.leftText: Look! The hand of My betrayer is with Mine on the table.
units.rightText: But behold, the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table.

units.leftText: Indeed, the Son of Man will go as it has been determined, but woe to that man who betrays Him.”
units.rightText: For the Son of man indeed goeth, as it hath been determined: but woe unto that man through whom he is betrayed!

units.leftText: Then they began to question among themselves which of them was going to do this. Who Is the Greatest?
units.rightText: And they began to question among themselves, which of them it was that should do this thing.

units.leftText: A dispute also arose among the disciples as to which of them should be considered the greatest.
units.rightText: And there arose also a contention among them, which of them was accounted to be greatest.

units.leftText: So Jesus declared, “The kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those in authority over them call themselves benefactors.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, The kings of the Gentiles have lordship over them; and they that have authority over them are called Benefactors.

units.leftText: But you shall not be like them. Instead, the greatest among you should be like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves.
units.rightText: But ye shall not be so: but he that is the greater among you, let him become as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve.

units.leftText: For who is greater, the one who reclines at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines? But I am among you as one who serves.
units.rightText: For which is greater, he that sitteth at meat, or he that serveth? is not he that sitteth at meat? but I am in the midst of you as he that serveth.

units.leftText: You are the ones who have stood by Me in My trials.
units.rightText: But ye are they that have continued with me in my temptations;

units.leftText: And I bestow on you a kingdom, just as My Father has bestowed one on Me,
units.rightText: and I appoint unto you a kingdom, even as my Father appointed unto me,

units.leftText: so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom and sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial (Matthew 26:31–35|MAT 26:31-35*; Mark 14:27–31|MRK 14:27-31*; John 13:36–38|JHN 13:36-38*)
units.rightText: that ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom; and ye shall sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

units.leftText: Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift all of you like wheat.
units.rightText: Simon, Simon, behold, Satan asked to have you, that he might sift you as wheat:

units.leftText: But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”
units.rightText: but I made supplication for thee, that thy faith fail not; and do thou, when once thou hast turned again, establish thy brethren.

units.leftText: “Lord,” said Peter, “I am ready to go with You even to prison and to death.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Lord, with thee I am ready to go both to prison and to death.

units.leftText: But Jesus replied, “I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today until you have denied three times that you know Me.”
units.rightText: And he said, I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, until thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.

units.leftText: Then Jesus asked them, “When I sent you out without purse or bag or sandals, did you lack anything?” “Nothing,” they answered.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, When I sent you forth without purse, and wallet, and shoes, lacked ye anything? And they said, Nothing.

units.leftText: “Now, however,” He told them, “the one with a purse should take it, and likewise a bag; and the one without a sword should sell his cloak and buy one.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, But now, he that hath a purse, let him take it, and likewise a wallet; and he that hath none, let him sell his cloak, and buy a sword.

units.leftText: For I tell you that this Scripture must be fulfilled in Me: ‘And He was numbered with the transgressors.’ For what is written about Me is reaching its fulfillment.”
units.rightText: For I say unto you, that this which is written must be fulfilled in me, And he was reckoned with transgressors: for that which concerneth me hath fulfilment.

units.leftText: So they said, “Look, Lord, here are two swords.” “That is enough,” He answered. Jesus Prays on the Mount of Olives (Matthew 26:36–46|MAT 26:36-46*; Mark 14:32–42|MRK 14:32-42*)
units.rightText: And they said, Lord, behold, here are two swords. And he said unto them, It is enough.

units.leftText: Jesus went out as usual to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples followed Him.
units.rightText: And he came out, and went, as his custom was, unto the mount of Olives; and the disciples also followed him.

units.leftText: When He came to the place, He told them, “Pray that you will not enter into temptation.”
units.rightText: And when he was at the place, he said unto them, Pray that ye enter not into temptation.

units.leftText: And He withdrew about a stone’s throw beyond them, where He knelt down and prayed,
units.rightText: And he was parted from them about a stone’s cast; and he kneeled down and prayed,

units.leftText: “Father, if You are willing, take this cup from Me. Yet not My will, but Yours be done.”
units.rightText: saying, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.

units.leftText: Then an angel from heaven appeared to Him and strengthened Him.
units.rightText: And there appeared unto him an angel from heaven, strengthening him.

units.leftText: And in His anguish, He prayed more earnestly, and His sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground.
units.rightText: And being in an agony he prayed more earnestly; and his sweat became as it were great drops of blood falling down upon the ground.
leftNotes: 22:44 Some manuscripts do not include verses 43 and 44.

units.leftText: When Jesus rose from prayer and returned to the disciples, He found them asleep, exhausted from sorrow.
units.rightText: And when he rose up from his prayer, he came unto the disciples, and found them sleeping for sorrow,

units.leftText: “Why are you sleeping?” He asked. “Get up and pray so that you will not enter into temptation.” The Betrayal of Jesus (Matthew 26:47–56|MAT 26:47-56*; Mark 14:43–52|MRK 14:43-52*; John 18:1–14|JHN 18:1-14*)
units.rightText: and said unto them, Why sleep ye? rise and pray, that ye enter not into temptation.

units.leftText: While He was still speaking, a crowd arrived, led by the man called Judas, one of the Twelve. He approached Jesus to kiss Him.
units.rightText: While he yet spake, behold, a multitude, and he that was called Judas, one of the twelve, went before them; and he drew near unto Jesus to kiss him.

units.leftText: But Jesus asked him, “Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?”
units.rightText: But Jesus said unto him, Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?

units.leftText: Those around Jesus saw what was about to happen and said, “Lord, should we strike with our swords?”
units.rightText: And when they that were about him saw what would follow, they said, Lord, shall we smite with the sword?

units.leftText: And one of them struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear.
units.rightText: And a certain one of them smote the servant of the high priest, and struck off his right ear.

units.leftText: But Jesus answered, “No more of this!” And He touched the man’s ear and healed him.
units.rightText: But Jesus answered and said, Suffer ye them thus far. And he touched his ear, and healed him.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to the chief priests, temple officers, and elders who had come for Him, “Have you come out with swords and clubs as you would against an outlaw?
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto the chief priests, and captains of the temple, and elders, that were come against him, Are ye come out, as against a robber, with swords and staves?

units.leftText: Every day I was with you in the temple courts, and you did not lay a hand on Me. But this hour belongs to you and to the power of darkness.” Peter Denies Jesus (Matthew 26:69–75|MAT 26:69-75*; Mark 14:66–72|MRK 14:66-72*; John 18:15–18|JHN 18:15-18*)
units.rightText: When I was daily with you in the temple, ye stretched not forth your hands against me: but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.
leftNotes: 22:53 Literally the temple

units.leftText: Then they seized Jesus, led Him away, and took Him into the house of the high priest. And Peter followed at a distance.
units.rightText: And they seized him, and led him away, and brought him into the high priest’s house. But Peter followed afar off.

units.leftText: When those present had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat down among them.
units.rightText: And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the court, and had sat down together, Peter sat in the midst of them.

units.leftText: A servant girl saw him seated in the firelight and looked intently at him. “This man also was with Him,” she said.
units.rightText: And a certain maid seeing him as he sat in the light of the fire, and looking stedfastly upon him, said, This man also was with him.

units.leftText: But Peter denied it. “Woman, I do not know Him,” he said.
units.rightText: But he denied, saying, Woman, I know him not.

units.leftText: A short time later, someone else saw him and said, “You also are one of them.” But Peter said, “Man, I am not.”
units.rightText: And after a little while another saw him, and said, Thou also art one of them. But Peter said, Man, I am not.

units.leftText: About an hour later, another man insisted, “Certainly this man was with Him, for he too is a Galilean.”
units.rightText: And after the space of about one hour another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this man also was with him; for he is a Galilæan.

units.leftText: “Man, I do not know what you are talking about,” Peter replied.
units.rightText: But Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.

units.leftText: And the Lord turned and looked at Peter.
units.rightText: And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how that he said unto him, Before the cock crow this day thou shalt deny me thrice.

units.leftText: And he went outside and wept bitterly. The Soldiers Mock Jesus (Isaiah 50:4–11|ISA 50:4-11*; Matthew 27:27–31|MAT 27:27-31*; Mark 15:16–20|MRK 15:16-20*; John 19:1–15|JHN 19:1-15*)
units.rightText: And he went out, and wept bitterly.

units.leftText: The men who were holding Jesus began to mock Him and beat Him.
units.rightText: And the men that held Jesus mocked him, and beat him.

units.leftText: They blindfolded Him and kept demanding, “Prophesy! Who hit You?”
units.rightText: And they blindfolded him, and asked him, saying, Prophesy: who is he that struck thee?
leftNotes: 22:64 BYZ and TR include and were striking Him on the face.

units.leftText: And they said many other blasphemous things against Him. Jesus before the Sanhedrin (Matthew 26:57–68|MAT 26:57-68*; Mark 14:53–65|MRK 14:53-65*; John 18:19–24|JHN 18:19-24*)
units.rightText: And many other things spake they against him, reviling him.

units.leftText: At daybreak the council of the elders of the people, both the chief priests and scribes, met together. They led Jesus into their Sanhedrin and said,
units.rightText: And as soon as it was day, the assembly of the elders of the people was gathered together, both chief priests and scribes; and they led him away into their council, saying,
leftNotes: 22:66 Or their Council

units.leftText: “If You are the Christ, tell us.”
units.rightText: If thou art the Christ, tell us. But he said unto them, If I tell you, ye will not believe:

units.leftText: And if I ask you a question, you will not answer.
units.rightText: and if I ask you, ye will not answer.

units.leftText: But from now on the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
units.rightText: But from henceforth shall the Son of man be seated at the right hand of the power of God.

units.leftText: So they all asked, “Are You then the Son of God?” He replied, “You say that I am.”
units.rightText: And they all said, Art thou then the Son of God? And he said unto them, Ye say that I am.

units.leftText: “Why do we need any more testimony?” they declared. “We have heard it for ourselves from His own lips.”
units.rightText: And they said, What further need have we of witness? for we ourselves have heard from his own mouth.

units.leftText: Then the whole council rose and led Jesus away to Pilate.
units.rightText: And the whole company of them rose up, and brought him before Pilate.

units.leftText: And they began to accuse Him, saying, “We found this man subverting our nation, forbidding payment of taxes to Caesar, and proclaiming Himself to be Christ, a King.”
units.rightText: And they began to accuse him, saying, We found this man perverting our nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Cæsar, and saying that he himself is Christ a king.

units.leftText: So Pilate asked Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.
units.rightText: And Pilate asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answered him and said, Thou sayest.

units.leftText: Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, “I find no basis for a charge against this man.”
units.rightText: And Pilate said unto the chief priests and the multitudes, I find no fault in this man.

units.leftText: But they kept insisting, “He stirs up the people all over Judea with His teaching. He began in Galilee and has come all the way here.” Jesus before Herod
units.rightText: But they were the more urgent, saying, He stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Judæa, and beginning from Galilee even unto this place.

units.leftText: When Pilate heard this, he asked if the man was a Galilean.
units.rightText: But when Pilate heard it, he asked whether the man were a Galilæan.

units.leftText: And learning that Jesus was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herod, who himself was in Jerusalem at that time.
units.rightText: And when he knew that he was of Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him unto Herod, who himself also was at Jerusalem in these days.

units.leftText: When Herod saw Jesus, he was greatly pleased. He had wanted to see Him for a long time, because he had heard about Him and was hoping to see Him perform a miracle.
units.rightText: Now when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceeding glad: for he was of a long time desirous to see him, because he had heard concerning him; and he hoped to see some miracle done by him.

units.leftText: Herod questioned Jesus at great length, but He gave no answer.
units.rightText: And he questioned him in many words; but he answered him nothing.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, the chief priests and scribes stood there, vehemently accusing Him.
units.rightText: And the chief priests and the scribes stood, vehemently accusing him.

units.leftText: And even Herod and his soldiers ridiculed and mocked Him. Dressing Him in a fine robe, they sent Him back to Pilate.
units.rightText: And Herod with his soldiers set him at nought, and mocked him, and arraying him in gorgeous apparel sent him back to Pilate.

units.leftText: That day Herod and Pilate became friends; before this time they had been enemies. The Crowd Chooses Barabbas (Matthew 27:15–23|MAT 27:15-23*; Mark 15:6–11|MRK 15:6-11*)
units.rightText: And Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that very day: for before they were at enmity between themselves.

units.leftText: Then Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,
units.rightText: And Pilate called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,

units.leftText: and said to them, “You brought me this man as one who was inciting the people to rebellion. I have examined Him here in your presence and found Him not guilty of your charges against Him.
units.rightText: and said unto them, Ye brought unto me this man, as one that perverteth the people: and behold, I, having examined him before you, found no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him:

units.leftText: Neither has Herod, for he sent Him back to us. As you can see, He has done nothing deserving of death.
units.rightText: no, nor yet Herod: for he sent him back unto us; and behold, nothing worthy of death hath been done by him.

units.leftText: Therefore I will punish Him and release Him.”
units.rightText: I will therefore chastise him, and release him.
leftNotes: 23:16 BYZ and TR include 17*Now Pilate was obligated to release to the people one prisoner at the feast; see Matthew 27:15|MAT 27:15* and Mark 15:6.

rightNotes: 23:17 Many ancient authorities insert v. 17. Now he must needs release unto them at the feast one prisoner. Comp. Mat 27:15; Mrk 15:6; Jhn 18:39. Others add the same words after v. 19.

units.leftText: But they all cried out in unison: “Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!”
units.rightText: But they cried out all together, saying, Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas:—

units.leftText: (Barabbas had been imprisoned for an insurrection in the city, and for murder.)
units.rightText: one who for a certain insurrection made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.

units.leftText: Wanting to release Jesus, Pilate addressed them again,
units.rightText: And Pilate spake unto them again, desiring to release Jesus;

units.leftText: but they kept shouting, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!”
units.rightText: but they shouted, saying, Crucify, crucify him.

units.leftText: A third time he said to them, “What evil has this man done? I have found in Him no offense worthy of death. So after I punish Him, I will release Him.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them the third time, Why, what evil hath this man done? I have found no cause of death in him: I will therefore chastise him and release him.

units.leftText: But they were insistent, demanding with loud voices for Jesus to be crucified. And their clamor prevailed.
units.rightText: But they were urgent with loud voices, asking that he might be crucified. And their voices prevailed.
leftNotes: 23:23 BYZ and TR include and that of the chief priests.

units.leftText: So Pilate sentenced that their demand be met.
units.rightText: And Pilate gave sentence that what they asked for should be done.

units.leftText: As they had requested, he released the one imprisoned for insurrection and murder, and he handed Jesus over to their will. The Crucifixion (Psalm 22:1–31|PSA 22:1-31*; Matthew 27:32–44|MAT 27:32-44*; Mark 15:21–32|MRK 15:21-32*; John 19:16–27|JHN 19:16-27*)
units.rightText: And he released him that for insurrection and murder had been cast into prison, whom they asked for; but Jesus he delivered up to their will.

units.leftText: As the soldiers led Him away, they seized Simon of Cyrene on his way in from the country, and they put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
units.rightText: And when they led him away, they laid hold upon one Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, and laid on him the cross, to bear it after Jesus.

units.leftText: A great number of people followed Him, including women who kept mourning and wailing for Him.
units.rightText: And there followed him a great multitude of the people, and of women who bewailed and lamented him.

units.leftText: But Jesus turned to them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
units.rightText: But Jesus turning unto them said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.

units.leftText: Look, the days are coming when people will say, ‘Blessed are the barren women, the wombs that never bore, and breasts that never nursed!’
units.rightText: For behold, the days are coming, in which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the breasts that never gave suck.

units.leftText: At that time ‘they will say to the mountains, “Fall on us!” and to the hills, “Cover us!”’
units.rightText: Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us.

units.leftText: For if men do these things while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?”
units.rightText: For if they do these things in the green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

units.leftText: Two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with Jesus.
units.rightText: And there were also two others, malefactors, led with him to be put to death.

units.leftText: When they came to the place called The Skull, they crucified Him there, along with the criminals, one on His right and the other on His left.
units.rightText: And when they came unto the place which is called The skull, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand and the other on the left.
leftNotes: 23:33 Greek Kranion; Vulgate Calvariae, rendered in some translations as Calvary

units.leftText: Then Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they divided up His garments by casting lots.
units.rightText: And Jesus said, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And parting his garments among them, they cast lots.
leftNotes: 23:34 Some manuscripts do not include Then Jesus said, “Father... what they are doing.”

units.leftText: The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered at Him, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”
units.rightText: And the people stood beholding. And the rulers also scoffed at him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God, his chosen.
leftNotes: 23:35 See Psalm 22:7|PSA 22:7*.

units.leftText: The soldiers also mocked Him and came up to offer Him sour wine.
units.rightText: And the soldiers also mocked him, coming to him, offering him vinegar,
leftNotes: 23:36 Or to offer Him wine vinegar

units.leftText: “If You are the King of the Jews,” they said, “save Yourself!”
units.rightText: and saying, If thou art the King of the Jews, save thyself.

units.rightText: And there was also a superscription over him, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
leftNotes: 23:38 BYZ and TR include written in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew; see John 19:20|JHN 19:20*.

units.leftText: One of the criminals who hung there heaped abuse on Him. “Are You not the Christ?” he said. “Save Yourself and us!”
units.rightText: And one of the malefactors that were hanged railed on him, saying, Art not thou the Christ? save thyself and us.

units.leftText: But the other one rebuked him, saying, “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same judgment?
units.rightText: But the other answered, and rebuking him said, Dost thou not even fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?

units.leftText: We are punished justly, for we are receiving what our actions deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong.”
units.rightText: And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.

units.leftText: Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!”
units.rightText: And he said, Jesus, remember me when thou comest in thy kingdom.
leftNotes: 23:42 BYZ and TR said to Jesus, “Remember me, Lord,

units.leftText: And Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.” The Death of Jesus (Psalm 31:1–24|PSA 31:1-24*; Matthew 27:45–56|MAT 27:45-56*; Mark 15:33–41|MRK 15:33-41*; John 19:28–30|JHN 19:28-30*)
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To-day shalt thou be with me in Paradise.

units.leftText: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
units.rightText: And it was now about the sixth hour, and a darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour,
leftNotes: 23:44 That is, from noon until three in the afternoon

units.leftText: Then Jesus called out in a loud voice, “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.” And when He had said this, He breathed His last.
units.rightText: And Jesus, crying with a loud voice, said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said this, he gave up the ghost.

units.leftText: When the centurion saw what had happened, he gave glory to God, saying, “Surely this was a righteous man. ”
units.rightText: And when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.

units.rightText: And all the multitudes that came together to this sight, when they beheld the things that were done, returned smiting their breasts.

units.rightText: And all his acquaintance, and the women that followed with him from Galilee, stood afar off, seeing these things.

units.rightText: And behold, a man named Joseph, who was a councillor, a good and righteous man

units.rightText: (he had not consented to their counsel and deed), a man of Arimathæa, a city of the Jews, who was looking for the kingdom of God:

units.leftText: He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
units.rightText: this man went to Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus.

units.leftText: Then he took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and placed it in a tomb cut into the rock, where no one had yet been laid.
units.rightText: And he took it down, and wrapped it in a linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb that was hewn in stone, where never man had yet lain.

units.leftText: It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was beginning.
units.rightText: And it was the day of the Preparation, and the sabbath drew on.
leftNotes: 23:54 Or was about to begin

units.leftText: The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed, and they saw the tomb and how His body was placed.
units.rightText: And the women, who had come with him out of Galilee, followed after, and beheld the tomb, and how his body was laid.

units.leftText: Then they returned to prepare spices and perfumes. And they rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment.
units.rightText: And they returned, and prepared spices and ointments. And on the sabbath they rested according to the commandment.

units.leftText: On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared.
units.rightText: But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they came unto the tomb, bringing the spices which they had prepared.
leftNotes: 24:1 Literally But on the first of the Sabbaths,

units.leftText: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
units.rightText: And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.

units.leftText: but when they entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
units.rightText: And they entered in, and found not the body of the Lord Jesus.

units.leftText: While they were puzzling over this, suddenly two men in radiant apparel stood beside them.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, while they were perplexed thereabout, behold, two men stood by them in dazzling apparel:

units.leftText: As the women bowed their faces to the ground in terror, the two men asked them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?
units.rightText: and as they were affrighted and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said unto them, Why seek ye the living among the dead?

units.leftText: He is not here; He has risen! Remember how He told you while He was still in Galilee:
units.rightText: He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee,

units.leftText: ‘The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.’”
units.rightText: saying that the Son of man must be delivered up into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.

units.leftText: Then they remembered His words.
units.rightText: And they remembered his words,

units.leftText: And when they returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the Eleven and to all the others.
units.rightText: and returned from the tomb, and told all these things to the eleven, and to all the rest.

units.leftText: It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told this to the apostles.
units.rightText: Now they were Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James: and the other women with them told these things unto the apostles.

units.leftText: But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.
units.rightText: And these words appeared in their sight as idle talk; and they disbelieved them.

units.leftText: Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb. And after bending down and seeing only the linen cloths, he went away, wondering to himself what had happened. The Road to Emmaus (Mark 16:12–13|MRK 16:12-13*)
units.rightText: But Peter arose, and ran unto the tomb; and stooping and looking in, he seeth the linen cloths by themselves; and he departed to his home, wondering at that which was come to pass.

units.leftText: That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And behold, two of them were going that very day to a village named Emmaus, which was threescore furlongs from Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 24:13 Greek being sixty stadia in distance; that is, approximately 6.9 miles or 11.1 kilometers

units.leftText: They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.
units.rightText: And they communed with each other of all these things which had happened.

units.leftText: And as they talked and deliberated, Jesus Himself came up and walked along with them.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, while they communed and questioned together, that Jesus himself drew near, and went with them.

units.leftText: But their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.
units.rightText: But their eyes were holden that they should not know him.

units.leftText: He asked them, “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, What communications are these that ye have one with another, as ye walk? And they stood still, looking sad.

units.leftText: One of them, named Cleopas, asked Him, “Are You the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in recent days?”
units.rightText: And one of them, named Cleopas, answering said unto him, Dost thou alone sojourn in Jerusalem and not know the things which are come to pass there in these days?

units.leftText: “What things?” He asked.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people:

units.leftText: Our chief priests and rulers delivered Him up to the sentence of death, and they crucified Him.
units.rightText: and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him up to be condemned to death, and crucified him.

units.leftText: But we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, it is the third day since these things took place.
units.rightText: But we hoped that it was he who should redeem Israel. Yea and besides all this, it is now the third day since these things came to pass.

units.leftText: Furthermore, some of our women astounded us. They were at the tomb early this morning,
units.rightText: Moreover certain women of our company amazed us, having been early at the tomb;

units.leftText: but they did not find His body. They came and told us they had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.
units.rightText: and when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, who said that he was alive.

units.leftText: Then some of our companions went to the tomb and found it just as the women had described. But Him they did not see.”
units.rightText: And certain of them that were with us went to the tomb, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to them, “O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
units.rightText: And he said unto them, O foolish men, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!

units.leftText: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?”
units.rightText: Behooved it not the Christ to suffer these things, and to enter into his glory?

units.leftText: And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.
units.rightText: And beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he interpreted to them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.

units.leftText: As they approached the village where they were headed, He seemed to be going farther.
units.rightText: And they drew nigh unto the village, whither they were going: and he made as though he would go further.

units.leftText: But they pleaded with Him, “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening and the day is almost over.”
units.rightText: And they constrained him, saying, Abide with us; for it is toward evening, and the day is now far spent. And he went in to abide with them.

units.leftText: While He was reclining at the table with them, He took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to them.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he had sat down with them to meat, he took the bread and blessed; and breaking it he gave to them.

units.leftText: Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Jesus — and He disappeared from their sight.
units.rightText: And their eyes were opened, and they knew him; and he vanished out of their sight.

units.leftText: They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”
units.rightText: And they said one to another, Was not our heart burning within us, while he spake to us in the way, while he opened to us the scriptures?

units.leftText: And they got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And they rose up that very hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and them that were with them,

units.leftText: and saying, “The Lord has indeed risen and has appeared to Simon!”
units.rightText: saying, The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon.

units.leftText: Then the two told what had happened on the road, and how they had recognized Jesus in the breaking of the bread. Jesus Appears to the Disciples (John 20:19–23|JHN 20:19-23*; 1 John 1:1–4|1JN 1:1-4*)
units.rightText: And they rehearsed the things that happened in the way, and how he was known of them in the breaking of the bread.

units.leftText: While they were describing these events, Jesus Himself stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
units.rightText: And as they spake these things, he himself stood in the midst of them, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.

units.leftText: But they were startled and frightened, thinking they had seen a spirit.
units.rightText: But they were terrified and affrighted, and supposed that they beheld a spirit.

units.leftText: “Why are you troubled,” Jesus asked, “and why do doubts arise in your hearts?
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Why are ye troubled? and wherefore do questionings arise in your heart?

units.leftText: Look at My hands and My feet. It is I Myself. Touch Me and see — for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.”
units.rightText: See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye behold me having.

units.leftText: And when He had said this, He showed them His hands and feet.
units.rightText: And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.

units.leftText: While they were still in disbelief because of their joy and amazement, He asked them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
units.rightText: And while they still disbelieved for joy, and wondered, he said unto them, Have ye here anything to eat?

units.leftText: So they gave Him a piece of broiled fish,
units.rightText: And they gave him a piece of a broiled fish.
leftNotes: 24:42 BYZ and TR include and some honeycomb.

units.leftText: and He took it and ate it in front of them.
units.rightText: And he took it, and ate before them.

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, These are my words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must needs be fulfilled, which are written in the law of Moses, and the prophets, and the psalms, concerning me.

units.leftText: Then He opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
units.rightText: Then opened he their mind, that they might understand the scriptures;

units.leftText: And He told them, “This is what is written: The Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
units.rightText: and he said unto them, Thus it is written, that the Christ should suffer, and rise again from the dead the third day;

units.leftText: and in His name repentance and forgiveness of sins will be proclaimed to all nations, beginning in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name unto all the nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 24:47 NA, NE, and WH repentance for

units.leftText: You are witnesses of these things.
units.rightText: Ye are witnesses of these things.

units.leftText: And behold, I am sending the promise of My Father upon you. But remain in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high.” The Ascension (Mark 16:19–20|MRK 16:19-20*; Acts 1:6–11|ACT 1:6-11*)
units.rightText: And behold, I send forth the promise of my Father upon you: but tarry ye in the city, until ye be clothed with power from on high.

units.leftText: When Jesus had led them out as far as Bethany, He lifted up His hands and blessed them.
units.rightText: And he led them out until they were over against Bethany: and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them.

units.leftText: While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he parted from them, and was carried up into heaven.

units.leftText: And they worshiped Him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
units.rightText: And they worshipped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy:

units.leftText: praising God continually in the temple.
units.rightText: and were continually in the temple, blessing God.
